cards.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
cards.definition: The open standard for plugging AI apps into tools and data: write one server and every MCP client can use it.
cards.hiDefinition: AI ऐप्स को टूल्स और डेटा से जोड़ने का खुला मानक: एक सर्वर लिखें, हर MCP क्लाइंट उसे इस्तेमाल कर सकता है।
points: Servers expose tools (actions), resources (data) and prompts (templates).
Runs locally over stdio or remotely over Streamable HTTP with OAuth.
Supported by Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and most agent frameworks.
useCases: Let an assistant query your database or tickets
Give a coding agent access to docs and issue trackers

industries.problem: One integration instead of a custom plugin per AI client
Governed, auditable access to internal systems

cards.title: Agent Skills
cards.definition: Folders of instructions, scripts and references that an agent loads only when a task needs them.
cards.hiDefinition: निर्देशों, स्क्रिप्ट और संदर्भों के फ़ोल्डर, जिन्हें एजेंट तभी लोड करता है जब काम को उनकी ज़रूरत हो।
points: Each skill is a SKILL.md with a name and description; the body loads on demand.
Progressive disclosure keeps context small even with many skills installed.
An open format, so one skill works across compatible agents.
useCases: Package your team's release checklist for an agent
Teach an agent to fill company document templates

industries.problem: Repeatable report formats without re-prompting each time
House conventions applied the same way by every agent

cards.title: A2A vs. MCP
cards.definition: A protocol for agents built by different teams and frameworks to discover each other and hand off work.
cards.hiDefinition: अलग-अलग टीमों और फ़्रेमवर्क से बने एजेंटों को एक-दूसरे को खोजने और काम सौंपने का प्रोटोकॉल।
points: Agents publish an Agent Card describing skills, endpoint and auth.
Work is modelled as tasks with states, messages and artifacts.
Complements MCP: MCP links agents to tools, A2A links agents to agents.
useCases: A travel agent delegating payment to a billing agent
Vendor agents cooperating inside one workflow

industries.problem: Partner agents coordinate orders without bespoke APIs
Agents from different vendors interoperate

compare.heading: MCP
compare.title: Agent ↔ tools & data
compare.summary: Connects one agent to the tools, resources and prompts it needs.
points: Client–server: the agent calls the server's tools.
The server is a capability, not a peer that plans.
compare.useWhen: An agent needs an API, database or file system.

compare.heading: A2A
compare.title: Agent ↔ agent
compare.summary: Lets independent agents discover each other and delegate whole tasks.
points: Agent Cards advertise skills; work flows as tasks with states.
Each agent stays opaque: it shares results, not internals.
compare.useWhen: Work must be handed to another team's or vendor's agent.

cards.title: Workflows vs. agents
cards.definition: Start with the simplest pattern that works; use an autonomous agent only when the steps can't be predicted.
cards.hiDefinition: सबसे सरल पैटर्न से शुरू करें; स्वायत्त एजेंट तभी चुनें जब कदम पहले से तय न हो सकें।
points: Workflows follow fixed paths: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization.
Orchestrator–workers and evaluator–optimizer handle open-ended subtasks.
Agents loop on tool results from the environment until the goal is met.
useCases: Route support tickets to the right specialised prompt
Let an agent fix a bug across unknown files

industries.problem: Predictable cost and quality on high-volume queues
Open-ended tasks that no fixed script can cover

compare.heading: Workflows
compare.title: Predefined code paths
compare.summary: Models and tools orchestrated through steps you write in code.
points: Prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator–workers.
Predictable cost, latency and output; easy to test.
compare.useWhen: The steps are known ahead of time.

compare.heading: Agents
compare.title: Model-directed process
compare.summary: The model chooses its own steps and tools, looping on feedback from the environment.
points: Plans, acts, checks results, repeats until done or stopped.
Flexible but costlier; errors compound, so sandbox and add guardrails.
compare.useWhen: Open-ended problems where the steps can't be predicted.

cards.title: Context engineering
cards.definition: The successor to prompt engineering: deciding which tokens an agent sees at every step of a long task.
cards.hiDefinition: प्रॉम्प्ट इंजीनियरिंग का अगला कदम: लंबे काम के हर चरण में एजेंट कौन-से टोकन देखे, यह तय करना।
points: Context is finite: more tokens can mean worse recall, not better answers.
Load data just in time with tools instead of stuffing it in up front.
Use compaction, structured notes and sub-agents for long-horizon work.
useCases: Keep a multi-hour coding session on track
Answer from a large codebase without loading all of it

industries.problem: Long documents reviewed without losing earlier facts
Multi-step investigations that outgrow one window

cards.title: Coding agents in the terminal
cards.definition: Agents such as Claude Code read your repo, edit files, run commands and tests, then show you the diff.
cards.hiDefinition: Claude Code जैसे एजेंट आपकी रिपॉज़िटरी पढ़ते हैं, फ़ाइलें बदलते हैं, कमांड और टेस्ट चलाते हैं और बदलाव दिखाते हैं।
points: Permission modes decide what runs without asking you first.
Hooks, skills, sub-agents and MCP servers extend what it can do.
The same agent loop runs in CI and in your apps via the Agent SDK.
useCases: Migrate a codebase to a new framework version
Write and run tests for an untested module

industries.problem: Small teams ship and maintain more surface area
Large legacy migrations done in reviewable steps

cards.title: Computer use & browser agents
cards.definition: Models that see screenshots and drive a mouse and keyboard, for software that has no API.
cards.hiDefinition: मॉडल जो स्क्रीनशॉट देखकर माउस और कीबोर्ड चलाते हैं, उन सॉफ़्टवेयर के लिए जिनका कोई API नहीं।
points: The model returns actions (click, type, scroll); your code executes them.
Run it in a sandboxed VM or container, never your own desktop session.
Prefer an API or MCP tool when one exists: faster and more reliable.
useCases: Fill forms in a legacy portal with no API
Test a web app the way a user clicks through it

industries.problem: Data entry across old systems without integrations
End-to-end checks of flows that change often

cards.title: Evals for agents
cards.definition: Tests for non-deterministic systems: a dataset of tasks, a grader, and a score you track on every change.
cards.hiDefinition: अनिश्चित सिस्टम के टेस्ट: कामों का डेटासेट, एक जाँचकर्ता और हर बदलाव पर देखा जाने वाला स्कोर।
points: Write success criteria first: specific, measurable, tied to real use.
Mix code-based checks with model-graded rubrics where judgement is needed.
Grade the outcome; check the trajectory when tools have side effects.
useCases: Catch regressions before a prompt change ships
Compare two models on your own tasks

industries.problem: Evidence that answers stay safe after every update
Measured accuracy before automating decisions

cards.title: Prompt injection & agent security
cards.definition: Anything an agent reads can contain instructions. Design so a hijacked agent still can't do much damage.
cards.hiDefinition: एजेंट जो कुछ भी पढ़ता है उसमें निर्देश छिपे हो सकते हैं। ऐसा डिज़ाइन करें कि बहका हुआ एजेंट भी ज़्यादा नुकसान न कर सके।
points: Prompt injection tops the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.
Grant least privilege: scoped tokens, allow-listed tools, sandboxes.
Require human approval for irreversible or outward-facing actions.
useCases: An email agent that must not forward data on request
A browsing agent reading untrusted web pages

industries.problem: No unauthorised transfers from manipulated inputs
Customer data kept out of attacker-controlled channels

cards.title: Content safety and policy checks
cards.definition: Route uncertain cases through a defined policy without confusing moderation with factual verification.
points: Evaluate inputs and outputs against the application's content policy.
Define handling for blocked, uncertain and allowed cases.
Reassess policy checks when new tools or media are added.
useCases: Three-way routing for chat replies — a community assistant's draft goes through a policy classifier, where high-confidence hate speech is blocked, borderline text goes to a human queue, and clean text is sent.

Re-run policy checks after adding image upload — a support agent that only screened text gets a new vision tool, so the team adds image moderation and tests it against a set of unsafe sample screenshots.

industries.problem: Moderators can't read every comment an agent drafts or sees, so borderline posts need a defined review path instead of silent allow or block.
A tutoring agent for minors must keep self-harm and explicit content out of chats, and unclear cases need a set escalation to staff.

cards.title: Deep Agents harness
cards.definition: Use a fuller agent harness for context management, file access and delegated work.
points: Combine planning, file tools and delegation in one agent harness.
Configure backends and tool permissions for the deployment.
Trace long-running tasks to identify wasted work.
useCases: Repo-wide dependency audit — a harness agent plans the work, writes findings to scratch files, and delegates each service folder to a worker, keeping the main context small.
Sandboxed file permissions — a deployment mounts a project directory read-write but blocks shell and network tools, so the agent edits drafts without touching anything else.

industries.problem: Long market research tasks outgrow one context window; file notes and delegated workers keep sources and drafts organised.
Multi-hour pipeline debugging wastes steps on repeated reads; traces show which tool calls looped so the harness can be tuned.

cards.title: Hybrid retrieval and reranking
cards.definition: Combine keyword and semantic recall, then rank a bounded evidence set.
points: Combine lexical matching with semantic candidate retrieval.
Rerank a limited candidate set using the original question.
Apply access filters before supplying evidence to generation.
useCases: Error code plus paraphrase lookup — an IT helpdesk bot merges exact-match hits on "ERR_4012" with semantic hits on "login keeps looping", then reranks the top 30 against the question.
Permission-trimmed policy answers — an HR assistant retrieves benefits passages by keyword and embedding, drops documents the employee's role cannot read, then reranks only the allowed set.

industries.problem: Drug names and trial IDs need exact matches while symptom descriptions need semantic recall, and restricted study documents must be filtered out first.
Claims staff search by policy number and by loosely worded loss descriptions, and reranking surfaces the right clause from a bounded candidate set.

cards.title: Planning and task tracking
cards.definition: Break complex goals into inspectable steps and revise the plan when evidence changes.
points: Represent work as concrete tasks with observable completion criteria.
Update task status only after verifying the result.
Revise the plan when new evidence changes dependencies.

Making generated answers trustworthy — Retrieval, guardrails and evaluation are what stand between a demo and something allowed to face a customer.

cards.title: Deep-agent recovery and budgets
cards.definition: Test restart behavior and enforce resource limits across delegated work.
points: Persist progress so interrupted runs can resume useful work.
Cap model calls, tool retries and execution duration.
Report the completed steps when the budget stops a run.

cards.title: Hallucination and grounding
cards.definition: Distinguish fluent generation from claims supported by verifiable evidence.
points: Retrieve authoritative evidence for claims that need verification.
Require citations that actually support the associated statement.
Abstain when the available evidence cannot resolve the question.
useCases: Cited policy answers — a HR bot retrieves the current parental leave policy and only states a rule if the quoted passage supports it, linking the policy section.
Abstain on missing API docs — a coding assistant asked about a parameter absent from the retrieved SDK reference says it cannot confirm and points to the changelog.

industries.problem: Models can invent plausible case citations, so claims must trace to retrieved rulings that actually support them.
A fluent dosing answer may be unsupported, so agents must cite current guidelines or decline when evidence is missing.

cards.title: Fallbacks, retries and circuit breakers
cards.definition: Recover from provider outages without duplicating work or creating retry storms.
points: Retry transient provider failures with bounded backoff.
Open a circuit when repeated failures indicate an unhealthy provider.
Use fallbacks only when required capabilities remain compatible.
useCases: Idempotent retry on a 503 — a gateway retries a chat completion after a provider 503 with jittered backoff and a request key, so one user message never bills or runs tools twice.
Breaker trips on a degraded region — after repeated timeouts from one provider, the gateway stops sending traffic for 30 seconds and probes with a single request before closing.

industries.problem: A provider outage during a ticket spike could make clients retry in sync, so bounded backoff and a breaker keep replies flowing.
Clinical note summarizers need a backup model only if it supports the same structured output, or the fallback is skipped.

cards.title: Agent trajectory and outcome evals
cards.definition: Check both the actions taken and whether the requested result was actually achieved.
points: Inspect tool sequences as well as the final outcome.
Score unnecessary calls, unsafe actions and failed recoveries.
Verify external task results instead of trusting agent self-reports.
useCases: Refund agent audit — grade whether the agent looked up the order before refunding, then check the payment system to confirm the right amount was actually returned.
Deploy agent trajectory replay — score a CI agent's tool sequence for redundant retries and skipped rollback, then query the cluster to confirm the release is healthy.

industries.problem: An account-closure agent may report success while skipping a hold check, so evals compare its actions to policy and the ledger.
Password-reset agents can claim tickets are resolved after failed calls, so evals check the directory for the real account state.

Handle refusals or malformed responses before downstream actions.

cards.title: Subagent context isolation
cards.definition: Give each worker a focused task and return concise findings rather than all intermediate messages.
points: Give subagents a focused prompt and relevant evidence.
Keep unrelated conversation history out of delegated context.
Require concise results with references for the parent.
useCases: Log triage subagent — a parent agent hands one worker a failing deploy's logs and gets back a three-line root cause with file and line references.
Per-vendor contract check — each subagent reads one vendor agreement against a clause list and returns only the deviations with page citations.

industries.problem: Alert investigations flood the analyst agent with raw telemetry; isolated workers return only verdicts with event IDs.
Literature reviews across hundreds of papers overflow context; one worker per paper returns key findings with citations.

points: Move bulky tool output into retrievable files or stores.
Preserve decisions and source pointers when summarizing context.

Check generated values against domain constraints after generation.
Route invalid results into a bounded repair or failure path.

Test indirect injections hidden in tool responses.

cards.title: Query rewriting and decomposition
cards.definition: Improve retrieval with focused subqueries without inventing assumptions about the user.
points: Preserve user constraints while expanding ambiguous search terms.
Break compound questions into independently answerable subqueries.
Combine retrieved results without treating rewrites as facts.
useCases: Split a compound support question — a user asks about refund policy and shipping time for an EU order, and each part becomes its own search against the right knowledge base.
Expand vague product terms — "the new plan" becomes searches for the current plan names and pricing pages, while the user's region and budget limits stay in every query.

industries.problem: Tickets mix several issues, so one search misses half; separate subqueries retrieve each answer without altering the customer's stated details.
Questions combine jurisdiction, date and claim type; focused subqueries find relevant cases while keeping those limits instead of assuming them.

cards.category: Agentic AI with LangChain and LangGraph
cards.definition: Delegate bounded work with evidence, ownership and a clear final synthesis contract.
points: Assign each agent a bounded task and output contract.
Pass only evidence and permissions needed for that assignment.
Reconcile conflicting findings before producing the final answer.

cards.title: Rate limits and backpressure
cards.definition: Control concurrency and token throughput before upstream quotas are exceeded.
points: Limit concurrent requests and token consumption per caller.
Queue only work that can finish within its deadline.
Return actionable retry information when capacity is exhausted.
useCases: Per-team token budgets — a gateway gives each internal agent team its own tokens-per-minute bucket so one batch job cannot starve the shared provider quota.
Deadline-aware queueing — a gateway rejects a queued summarization request when expected wait plus generation time exceeds the caller's 20-second timeout.

industries.problem: A ticket backlog replay sends thousands of agent calls at once; concurrency caps keep live chats responsive instead of hitting provider 429s.
Overnight document analysis shares a model quota with advisors' tools, so per-caller token limits and retry-after hints protect daytime use.

cards.title: SQL and structured retrieval
cards.definition: Answer from authorized database rows with validated queries and explicit result limits.
points: Validate query structure and restrict accessible tables and columns.
Bind user values as parameters instead of concatenating SQL.
Limit returned rows and use read-only execution for retrieval.
useCases: Parameterized order status lookup — an agent turns "where is my order 8841?" into a SELECT with the ID bound as a parameter, limited to the caller's own rows.
Allowlisted sales report query — an analytics agent may read only the orders and regions tables, on a read-only replica, with LIMIT 100 and a statement timeout.

industries.problem: Advisors ask about balances and transactions in plain language, and queries must reach only authorized accounts and columns, never raw card data.
Dispatchers ask for late shipments by depot, and validated read-only queries with row limits return exact tracking rows without risking write access.

cards.title: Checkpoints and human approval
cards.category: Agentic AI with LangChain and LangGraph
cards.definition: Persist progress and pause consequential actions for explicit review.
points: Save execution checkpoints with a stable thread identifier.
Present the proposed consequential action before approval.
Resume from saved state with the recorded reviewer decision.
useCases: Approve a refund before it posts — a LangGraph support agent pauses before calling issue_refund, shows amount and order ID, and resumes on the reviewer's approve or reject.
Resume a paused run after a restart — a graph saves a checkpoint under thread ID "case-8841", so a reviewer's decision hours later continues from the saved step, not from scratch.

industries.problem: Agent-drafted wire transfers must not execute unreviewed, so the run pauses with payee and amount and records who approved.
An agent proposing a production database change needs an on-call engineer's sign-off, and a saved checkpoint lets the run resume after review.

Keep training and tuning examples out of the held-out set.
Version dataset changes and include hard negative examples.

cards.title: Workflows versus agents
cards.category: Agentic AI with LangChain and LangGraph
cards.definition: Choose fixed control flow when the steps are known and model-directed actions when necessary.
points: Use deterministic steps for known business rules.
Delegate uncertain action selection to a model only where needed.
Keep approval and termination rules outside model discretion.
useCases: Loan pre-screen router — fixed code checks income and credit thresholds, and a model handles only free-text applicant explanations that rules can't classify.
Research assistant with step cap — a model picks which search or calculator tool to call next, while code enforces a ten-step limit and the final report format.

industries.problem: Order returns follow set refund rules, but odd customer messages need judgement, so code runs the policy and a model chooses only among unclear cases.
Incident response mixes known runbook steps with unknown faults, so fixed steps handle restarts while a model investigates, with humans approving any production change.

cards.title: Prompt design and few-shot examples
cards.definition: Specify a task, constraints and examples that make the desired response testable.
points: Separate task instructions, constraints and reference material.
Show representative input-output pairs with consistent formatting.
Test prompts on edge cases outside the examples.
useCases: Ticket triage prompt with labeled examples — a support team puts the label list and rules in one block and three sample tickets with JSON outputs in another, then tests it on a ticket mixing two issues.
Edge-case test set for an extraction prompt — an engineer runs a date-parsing prompt against inputs like "next Fri", blank fields and mixed locales that none of the few-shot examples cover.

industries.problem: Product-listing prompts must map messy seller text to fixed attributes, and consistent examples keep size and color formats uniform.
Reply-drafting prompts drift in tone and policy, so separated rules plus sample replies make each draft checkable against a spec.

cards.definition: Combine text and supported media while respecting format and model capability limits.
points: Check which image, audio and video formats the model accepts.
Preserve media resolution and timestamps needed for the task.
Evaluate cross-modal claims against the original input.
useCases: Call recording QA — a model gets a support call's audio clip plus its transcript with timestamps, then flags where the agent skipped the required refund disclosure.
Unsupported format fallback — an upload step converts a user's .mov screen recording into accepted frames plus audio before sending it to a model that rejects that container.

industries.problem: Editors need clip summaries tied to exact timestamps, so a model can cite where each claimed scene appears in the footage.
Scan images and report text must be checked together at full resolution so downscaling does not hide findings the draft mentions.

cards.title: LangGraph state and reducers
cards.category: Agentic AI with LangChain and LangGraph
cards.definition: Model shared state and define how updates merge across graph branches.
points: Declare state fields and their update semantics explicitly.
Use reducers to combine concurrent updates to shared fields.
Keep non-mergeable writes on separate execution paths.
useCases: Parallel research branches merging findings — three search nodes run at once and a list reducer appends each result into one shared findings field instead of overwriting.
Chat history with message reducer — a support agent's state uses an add-messages reducer so tool calls and replies from different nodes append, and updates by message ID replace earlier ones.

industries.problem: Parallel scrapers write to one report field and overwrite each other unless a reducer merges their findings.
Several nodes update one ticket conversation at once, and a message reducer keeps every reply and tool result in order.

cards.title: Vectorless retrieval tradeoffs
cards.definition: Benchmark lexical, structural and vector retrieval on the same tasks instead of assuming a universal winner.
points: Use the same questions and permission filters for each approach.

cards.title: System, human and AI messages
cards.definition: Represent conversation roles explicitly instead of concatenating untrusted text into instructions.
points: Roles are represented as message objects rather than concatenated text.
Concatenating untrusted text into instructions is prompt injection by construction.
The role is what the model uses to weigh instruction against data.
useCases: Support bot guardrails — a helpdesk assistant keeps refund policy in a SystemMessage and passes the customer's pasted email as a HumanMessage, so embedded commands stay data.
Multi-turn history replay — a chat backend stores prior turns as HumanMessage and AIMessage objects so the model sees who said what when answering follow-ups.

industries.problem: Customer chat text can't override compliance instructions about disclosing balances when roles keep system rules separate from user input.
Uploaded contract clauses containing instruction-like wording are treated as human-supplied data, not as rules that change the review assistant's behavior.

cards.title: Structured output schemas
cards.definition: Define typed output contracts with required fields, allowed values and validation.
points: `response_format` takes a Pydantic model that validates the reply.
The parsed value is read from `result["structured_response"]`.
A reply that validates against the schema can still be semantically wrong.
useCases: Support ticket triage — an agent returns a Pydantic model with category as an enum, priority 1-5 and a required summary, so the helpdesk API can route it.
Invoice field extraction — pull vendor, due date and line items from scanned PDF text into typed fields, rejecting replies where the total is missing or not numeric.

industries.problem: Adjusters get free-text claim emails; a schema forces claim type and incident date into fields the policy system accepts.
Resumes come in varied formats; a typed schema with allowed seniority values lets candidates be filtered consistently in the ATS.

cards.title: LangChain vs LangGraph vs Deep Agents
cards.definition: Choose a configurable agent, custom state graph or fuller agent harness for the task.
points: A configurable agent, a custom state graph or a fuller harness suit different tasks.
Branching, persistence and approvals are what push a task toward a graph.
Starting with the heaviest option costs complexity the task may never need.
useCases: FAQ bot on a configurable agent — a support team ships a docs-search assistant with a model and two retrieval tools, no custom graph or persistence needed.
Refund workflow as a state graph — an order system routes by amount, pauses for manager approval, and resumes from a checkpoint after a day.

industries.problem: Simple order-lookup questions need a light agent, while refunds need approvals and resumable steps that justify a graph.
Long multi-document research needs planning, file-based notes and sub-agents, which a fuller harness provides without hand-built orchestration.

cards.title: LangChain architecture
cards.definition: Separate model integrations, agent behavior and the LangGraph runtime when designing an application.
points: Model integrations, agent behaviour and the graph runtime are separate layers.
Separating them is what lets a provider change without touching agent logic.
Treating the layers as one produces code that cannot be tested in pieces.
useCases: Provider swap behind a stable interface — a support-ticket triage agent moves from one hosted chat model to another by changing only the model integration config, not its tool-calling logic.
Unit-testing agent behavior with a fake model — a refund-approval agent's tool selection is tested against a stub chat model, with no network call or graph runtime needed.

industries.problem: Order-support agents must switch model providers for cost or latency without rewriting refund and returns logic.
Compliance reviews require testing intake-agent behavior in isolation from the model vendor and the durable execution runtime.

cards.title: Tool messages and call IDs
cards.definition: Pair every tool result with its originating call so the model can continue correctly.
points: Every tool result is paired with the call id that produced it.
The id is how the model matches a result to the request it made.
A missing or mismatched id breaks the conversation the model is reconstructing.
useCases: Parallel tool calls — an assistant requests weather and calendar lookups in one turn, and each ToolMessage carries its own tool_call_id so results aren't swapped.
Retry after tool failure — a flaky inventory API times out, so the agent returns a ToolMessage with the original call id and an error string for the model to react to.

industries.problem: A flight-and-hotel agent fires several searches at once and needs each price result matched to the right request.
A support bot calling order lookup and refund tools must not attach a refund status to the wrong order in the transcript.

cards.title: Multimodal content blocks
cards.definition: Pass supported image, audio and text blocks while respecting provider input constraints.
points: Image, audio and text blocks travel in one request where the provider supports it.
Support differs per provider, so a block that works on one fails on another.
Non-text blocks consume context, often far more than they appear to.
useCases: Receipt photo extraction — send a photographed expense receipt image block with a text instruction in one HumanMessage to return merchant, date and total as structured fields.
Voice note triage — attach a customer's recorded audio block alongside a text prompt so the model summarizes the complaint, with a check that the chosen provider accepts audio input.

industries.problem: Adjusters get damage photos plus written notes, and one request can pair both while resizing images to fit provider limits.
Patients send a rash photo and spoken symptoms, so mixed blocks reach one model without exceeding context or unsupported formats.

cards.title: Few-shot examples
cards.definition: Show representative input-output pairs without leaking evaluation answers into the prompt.
points: Representative input-output pairs demonstrate the task.
Examples usually teach format more reliably than instructions do.
Drawing them from the evaluation set leaks the answers being measured.
useCases: Ticket triage labels — a support classifier gets six held-out-safe ticket/label pairs in a FewShotChatMessagePromptTemplate so it returns exactly one of four queue names.
Log-to-JSON extraction — an ops tool shows three sample log lines with their target JSON so the model copies field names and nesting, with eval logs kept out of the example pool.

industries.problem: Adjuster notes need consistent coded summaries, and examples from past closed claims set the format without reusing test-set claims.
Product titles from many sellers must map to one category taxonomy, and sample pairs fix label wording while the benchmark listings stay unseen.

cards.title: Provider integration packages
cards.definition: Keep core interfaces separate from provider-specific model, tool and embedding implementations.
points: Core interfaces stay separate from provider-specific implementations.
The interface is what makes a provider swap a configuration change.
Provider-specific behaviour still leaks through, so a swap needs retesting.
useCases: Cloud-to-local model swap — a RAG service built on the chat model interface switches from a hosted API model to a self-hosted one by changing the installed package and config, then reruns its eval set.

Embedding provider migration — a search team swaps the embeddings class behind its vector store retriever, then re-embeds the corpus and rechecks recall because vector dimensions and similarity behavior differ.

industries.problem: A hospital must move a clinical note summarizer to an approved in-region provider without rewriting chains, while retesting tool-call and formatting quirks.
A product search team can trial cheaper embedding vendors behind one interface, avoiding rewrites while catching ranking changes before they reach shoppers.

cards.title: Token usage and context limits
cards.definition: Track input and output tokens, reserve response space and trim irrelevant history.
points: Input and output tokens are tracked and response space reserved.
Filling the window with history leaves no room for the answer.
Trimming has to keep tool calls and their results together to stay coherent.
useCases: Trimming long chat history — a coding assistant drops the oldest turns once the prompt nears the window, reserving a fixed output budget so the reply is never cut off.
Tool-call-safe trimming — a log-analysis agent trims history without separating an AIMessage's tool call from its ToolMessage result, avoiding an invalid message sequence.

industries.problem: Long ticket threads with pasted logs fill the window, so older turns must be trimmed while leaving room for the answer.
Incident agents that call many diagnostic tools pile up large results, so trimming must keep each call paired with its output.

cards.title: Graph compilation
cards.definition: Check graph structure and attach persistence and runtime options before execution.
points: Compiling validates the structure and produces something executable.
Validation at compile time catches an unreachable or dangling node.
The compiled graph is where the checkpointer and limits are attached.
useCases: Running an agent that survives a restart — State is checkpointed at each step, so a long-running task resumes rather than starting over when a process dies.
Requiring a human before an action lands — An interrupt pauses the graph for approval, which is what makes an agent safe to let near money, email or production data.

industries.problem: An agent that moves money needs a human approval step it cannot skip, which an interrupt in a durable graph enforces.
Claims triage runs for hours across several tools, so state has to survive a restart rather than living in one process's memory.

cards.title: Static edges
cards.definition: Connect deterministic stages whose next step is known before execution.
points: A fixed edge always routes from one node to the next.
Fixed routing is the part of the graph that needs no reasoning at runtime.
Every static edge is a decision taken at build time, not per run.
useCases: Running an agent that survives a restart — State is checkpointed at each step, so a long-running task resumes rather than starting over when a process dies.
Requiring a human before an action lands — An interrupt pauses the graph for approval, which is what makes an agent safe to let near money, email or production data.
