cards.title: Conditional edges
cards.definition: Route from validated state and handle every expected decision outcome.
points: A function inspects state and chooses the next node.
The choice is ordinary code, so it is testable without a model.
Returning a name that is not a node fails at run time, not at compile time.
useCases: Route a triage verdict — a classify node writes category=billing|technical|abuse to state, and a routing function maps each value to its own node with a fallback for unknown labels.
Unit-test the router without a model — a pytest feeds hand-built state dicts like {"score": 0.4} into the routing function and asserts it returns "escalate", so no LLM call is needed.

industries.problem: A symptom-intake graph must send red-flag answers to a nurse node and routine ones to scheduling, with no unhandled outcome.
Claim state with amount and fraud score must route to auto-approve, adjuster review or SIU, and a mistyped branch name would fail mid-run.

cards.title: LangGraph architecture
cards.definition: Model a workflow as state, nodes and transitions running on a durable execution engine.
points: Work is a graph of nodes over a shared state, not a linear chain.
The graph is data, which is what makes the path inspectable and resumable.
A chain cannot express a cycle; a graph is defined by being able to.
useCases: Research-and-critique loop — a writer node drafts an answer, a critic node scores it, and a conditional edge returns to the writer until the score passes or a retry cap is hit.
Inspect a stalled run — an engineer reads the compiled graph's nodes and edges plus the latest checkpoint to see which node an agent stopped at and why.

industries.problem: Code-fix agents must loop between patching and running tests until green, which a linear chain cannot express without hand-rolled retry code.
Long-running ticket workflows need an inspectable path and a resumable position, so a stuck case can be traced to a node and continued.

cards.title: StateGraph
cards.definition: Define a state schema, register nodes and compile the graph before invoking it.
points: Nodes, edges and a state schema are declared, then compiled into a runnable.
The schema is the contract every node reads and writes through.
A node that returns something outside the schema is dropped, not merged.
useCases: Typed state for a support triage graph — a StateGraph declares a TypedDict with messages, ticket_category and priority, so classify, retrieve and draft nodes all read and write the same fields.
Silent drop from a typo'd key — a draft node returns {"reply_text": ...} while the schema field is "draft", so the update is dropped and the review node sees an empty draft.

industries.problem: Claims intake graphs pass policy data, photos and fraud flags between steps, and a fixed state schema keeps every node using the same field names.
Resume screening agents pass candidate data between parse, score and outreach nodes, so a compiled graph with a declared schema keeps the pipeline consistent.

cards.title: START and END
cards.definition: Declare entry and terminal transitions so every execution path has a clear lifecycle.
points: Two sentinel nodes mark where execution enters and leaves.
They make entry and exit explicit rather than implied by declaration order.
A path with no route to END runs until a limit stops it.
useCases: Running an agent that survives a restart — State is checkpointed at each step, so a long-running task resumes rather than starting over when a process dies.
Requiring a human before an action lands — An interrupt pauses the graph for approval, which is what makes an agent safe to let near money, email or production data.

industries.problem: An agent that moves money needs a human approval step it cannot skip, which an interrupt in a durable graph enforces.
Claims triage runs for hours across several tools, so state has to survive a restart rather than living in one process's memory.

cards.title: LangGraph learning module
cards.definition: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework and runtime for building, managing and deploying long-running, stateful agents, with durable execution, streaming and human-in-the-loop built in.
points: State plus reducers define how node updates merge each super-step.
A checkpointer and a `thread_id` are required for memory, interrupts and recovery.
A resumed node re-runs from its start, so side effects before `interrupt` must be idempotent.
useCases: Agents that cannot pause, recover or be controlled — A plain agent loop lives in one process's memory: a crash or deploy loses the run, there is no safe place to stop for human approval, and branching logic ends up as prompt instructions the model may ignore. LangGraph makes control flow explicit code, persists state after every step so a run can resume after failure or days later, and turns human approval into a first-class `interrupt` rather than a polling hack.

Approval workflows in regulated operations — A bank's dispute-handling agent gathers evidence and drafts a decision, then interrupts for an analyst's sign-off. The checkpoint keeps the full state while the analyst reviews, possibly hours later, and resuming continues on the approved path with an audit trail of every step.

industries.problem: A claims agent pauses for adjuster review and must not resubmit the payout request when the node re-runs on resume.
Scores from parallel interviewer-summary nodes must combine into one list, not let the last branch overwrite the rest.

cards.title: LangSmith learning module
cards.definition: LangSmith is a framework-agnostic platform for developing, debugging, evaluating and deploying LLM applications and agents, combining tracing, evaluation, prompt engineering and deployment in one place.
points: A trace is a tree of runs; the tree shows which step caused the failure.
`@traceable` instruments any Python or TypeScript code, not only LangChain.
Datasets plus evaluators turn each change into a measured experiment.
useCases: Shipping LLM changes blind — Without LangSmith, a team debugging a bad agent answer has scattered logs with no view of which retrieval result or tool call caused it, and every prompt or model change is judged by a few manual spot checks. Regressions reach users first. LangSmith records the full execution tree for every request, lets you turn a failing production trace into a dataset example in a click, and runs experiments so each change is measured against the same examples before release.

Root-causing a wrong answer in a RAG assistant — A support lead flags a hallucinated policy answer. The engineer opens the trace, sees that the retriever returned an outdated document and the model faithfully summarized it, fixes the index, and adds the trace to the regression dataset so the case is tested forever after.

industries.problem: Fraud-dispute assistants must show which retrieved policy or tool call produced a wrong answer, so audits can trace each decision.
Tutoring agents give wrong hints after prompt tweaks, so teams need measured experiments on sample student questions before release.

cards.title: Prompt and Context Hub
cards.definition: Manage reusable prompt and context assets separately from application deployment.
points: Prompts are versioned centrally rather than embedded in code.
Central storage is what lets a prompt change without a deploy.
It also means a prompt can change without a code review.
useCases: Hotfix a tone problem live — A support bot starts sounding curt after a model update, so a prompt engineer edits the system prompt in the hub and the service pulls the new version without a deploy.
Roll back a bad prompt version — After a prompt edit raises refusal rates, the team repoints the production tag to the previous commit instead of reverting and redeploying application code.

industries.problem: Compliance wording in assistant prompts changes often, and a central versioned history shows who edited a live prompt and when, even without a code review.
Product managers must update seasonal policy text in itinerary-bot prompts quickly without waiting on an engineering release cycle.

cards.title: Manual run instrumentation
cards.definition: Create explicit run boundaries when automatic instrumentation does not fit the application.
points: Runs are created and closed explicitly through the client.
Explicit control is needed where execution does not fit a function boundary.
A run never closed stays pending and distorts the timings.
useCases: Seeing what an AI feature actually did — Every call, tool use, retrieval and token is traced, which is the only way to explain a bad answer after the fact.
Knowing whether a prompt change helped — A dataset and a scored run turn a change from an opinion into a measurement across the cases that matter.

industries.industry: Any team shipping an AI feature
industries.problem: A prompt change that helps ten cases and breaks thirty is invisible without a dataset and a scored run against it.
Quality complaints have to be traced to the exact call, retrieval and token spend that produced the bad answer.

cards.title: Multiturn evaluation datasets
cards.definition: Represent conversation history and expected outcomes for stateful agents.
points: A conversation, not a single input, is the unit of evaluation.
Multi-turn behaviour is where single-turn tests say nothing.
Each turn depends on the last, so the sequence cannot be shuffled.
useCases: Refund flow regression set — Each example stores a scripted customer exchange where the agent must collect an order ID, check eligibility, then confirm the refund, and the run is scored on the final state.
Memory of earlier turns — A dataset replays a user who states a dietary restriction in turn two and asks for a recipe in turn six, checking the agent still honours the restriction.

industries.problem: Plan-change bots must remember account details across many turns, which one-shot test questions never exercise.
Appointment agents must keep patient constraints through rescheduling turns, so tests need whole conversations with expected end bookings.

cards.title: Assistants, threads and runs
cards.definition: Separate configured agent behavior, conversation state and individual executions.
points: An assistant is a configured graph; threads hold conversations; runs are executions.
The separation is what lets one graph serve many configurations.
Thread state persists, so it must eventually be cleaned up.
useCases: Per-tenant assistant variants — Create several assistants from one support-triage graph, each with its own system prompt and model setting, so each customer gets tailored behavior without a redeploy.
Resuming a chat after a page reload — The frontend stores a thread ID and posts a new run to it, so the agent sees earlier messages and continues the conversation.

industries.problem: One shared agent graph must serve many customers with different prompts and tool limits without maintaining a separate deployment for each.
Long-running customer chats keep stored thread state, so agents need conversation continuity now and retention cleanup of old threads later.

cards.title: Deployment monitoring
cards.definition: Watch execution failures, capacity and downstream dependencies after a release.
points: Latency, errors, cost and feedback are watched in production.
Production is where the inputs you never imagined arrive.
A dashboard nobody reads is not monitoring.
useCases: Post-release error spike alert — After shipping a new agent version, an alert fires when the tool-call error rate in the production project exceeds its pre-release baseline, paging the on-call engineer.
Token cost per tenant drift — A platform team charts weekly token cost and p95 latency grouped by customer tag, spotting one tenant whose long documents push the agent past its budget.

industries.problem: A refund agent update passes tests, then fails on odd real order messages and a slow inventory API, so monitoring must surface it within minutes.
After a release, a booking agent's calls to an external calendar API start timing out, and alerts catch it before patients hit failed appointments.

cards.title: Custom evaluators
cards.definition: Score a run with your own function, which receives the run and the reference example.
points: A scoring function is written for a domain-specific property.
Generic evaluators miss what actually matters to a specific product.
A custom evaluator needs calibrating like any other.
useCases: Seeing what an AI feature actually did — Every call, tool use, retrieval and token is traced, which is the only way to explain a bad answer after the fact.
Knowing whether a prompt change helped — A dataset and a scored run turn a change from an opinion into a measurement across the cases that matter.

industries.industry: Any team shipping an AI feature
industries.problem: A prompt change that helps ten cases and breaks thirty is invisible without a dataset and a scored run against it.
Quality complaints have to be traced to the exact call, retrieval and token spend that produced the bad answer.

cards.title: Prompt versions and commits
cards.definition: Record changes to instructions and identify which version produced an output.
points: Each change is a commit with history.
History is what makes a rollback possible and a change attributable.
A version pinned nowhere means production can move underneath you.
useCases: Rollback after a tone regression — Support complaints rise after a system prompt edit, so the team compares commit history, finds the change, and restores the previous commit in the hub.
Pinning production to a commit — The deployed agent pulls its prompt by a specific commit hash instead of latest, so edits in the playground can't silently change live answers.

industries.problem: Auditors ask which exact loan-explanation prompt produced a customer reply, and commit history ties each output to a reviewed wording.
Several people edit one shared triage prompt, and without commits a sudden drop in routing accuracy can't be traced to a change.

cards.title: Automatic LangChain tracing
cards.definition: Capture framework calls with tracing configuration and inspect the generated run structure.
points: Enabling an environment variable traces every LangChain call.
Zero-code tracing is what makes adoption immediate.
It traces everything, including what should not be recorded.
useCases: Zero-code tracing rollout — Set the tracing environment variables on an existing LangChain service in staging and immediately see every chain, retriever and LLM call as nested runs, with no code changes.
Redacting sensitive inputs — After auto-tracing captures full prompts containing customer emails, the team inspects the run tree and adds input masking or turns tracing off for that chain.

industries.problem: Auto-tracing every chain call can store patient symptoms in traces, so teams must audit run inputs and mask them before enabling it.
A shopping assistant built on LangChain gets instant visibility into slow retriever and tool calls without engineers instrumenting each step.

cards.title: LangSmith deployment options
cards.definition: Compare hosted and self-managed deployment choices against operational and data requirements.
points: Cloud, hybrid and self-hosted differ in where data lives.
Data residency is usually what decides between them.
Self-hosting moves the operational burden onto your team.
useCases: Residency-driven hosting choice — An EU bank's agent traces contain account details that must stay in-region, so the platform team picks self-hosted LangSmith inside its own VPC over the SaaS cloud.

Hybrid split for a small team — A startup keeps the LangSmith control plane hosted for fast setup while agent runtime and trace payloads stay in its own cloud account, avoiding a full self-hosted cluster.

industries.problem: Traces with account data cannot leave approved regions, so deployment must keep trace storage inside the bank's own infrastructure.
Agencies on air-gapped or restricted networks cannot send prompts to a vendor cloud and must run and patch the platform themselves.

cards.title: Online evaluators
cards.definition: Apply selected quality checks to production runs under explicit sampling and cost limits.
points: Online evaluation targets production runs and threads rather than a dataset.
It has no reference outputs available, so evaluators must be reference-free.
Scoring live traffic adds a model call to the traffic being scored.
useCases: Sampled groundedness scoring — Run a reference-free hallucination check on 5% of production answers from a support RAG bot, capped per day to bound judge cost.
Thread-level frustration flag — Score whole chat threads once they go idle for a user-frustration evaluator, and alert when the failure rate climbs after a prompt release.

industries.problem: Compliance needs ongoing checks that live chatbot replies avoid giving financial advice, without paying to judge every conversation.
A tutoring assistant drifts on real student questions, and no reference answers exist to score them, so quality needs sampled live checks.

cards.title: traceable instrumentation
cards.definition: Wrap custom functions so their input, output and timing join the surrounding trace.
points: A decorator turns an ordinary function into a traced run.
Decorating is the cheapest way to trace code that is not a framework call.
Arguments and return values are captured, so sensitive data is captured too.
useCases: Tracing a custom reranker — Decorate the in-house function that reorders retrieved chunks so its inputs, scores and latency appear as a child run under the RAG request.
Timing a parsing step — Decorate the function that turns raw PDF text into structured fields so slow or failing extraction shows up as its own run inside the agent trace.

industries.problem: Claim-triage agents call in-house policy lookup code that framework tracing misses, so decorating it reveals which step slowed or altered a decision.
A route-planning assistant calls custom rate-calculation functions, and decorating them shows the inputs behind a bad shipping quote inside the trace.

cards.title: LangFlow learning module
cards.definition: Langflow is an open-source, Python-based tool for building and deploying AI-powered agents and workflows through a visual, low-code interface, where every flow can also be served as an API or exposed as an MCP server.
points: A flow is a graph of Python components connected by typed ports (Message, JSON, Table), saved as JSON.
Every flow is an API: `POST /api/v1/run/{flow_id}` with an `x-api-key` header.
Global variables keep secrets out of exported flows.
useCases: Slow iteration on AI pipelines locked inside code — Without Langflow, every experiment with a different splitter, embedding model, retriever setting or agent prompt means editing code, rerunning scripts and wiring a test UI, and product or domain experts cannot take part. Langflow makes the pipeline a visible graph that anyone on the team can rewire and test in the Playground in seconds, then serves the exact flow that was tested as an API, removing the rewrite between prototype and integration.

Internal RAG assistant from prototype to API — An HR team uploads policy PDFs; an engineer builds a flow of File loader, Split Text, Embeddings and a vector store, plus a retrieval chat flow. HR reviewers test answers in the Playground, and the intranet calls the flow's run endpoint with a per-employee `session_id`.

industries.problem: A policy assistant over company documents is needed in days, and a visual RAG flow served as an API removes the rewrite between prototype and integration.
Teams want their internal workflows callable from AI assistants, and publishing flows as MCP tools avoids writing a separate server for each.

cards.title: Your first flow: Basic Prompting
cards.definition: Connect Chat Input, a Prompt Template, a Language Model and Chat Output, then test it in the Playground.
points: Chat Input turns the user's text into a Message; Chat Output returns the reply.
The Prompt Template's `{variables}` become input ports you wire upstream outputs into.
Templates such as Basic Prompting and Simple Agent are starting points you copy and modify.
useCases: Prompt tweak in Playground — a developer edits the Prompt Template's system text in Basic Prompting and re-sends the same test message to compare replies before saving.
Wiring a new template variable — an engineer adds {tone} to a Prompt Template, sees a new input port appear, and connects a Text Input component to it.

industries.problem: Course teams need a working tutoring chatbot demo fast, so a Basic Prompting flow lets instructors test tutor prompts before any engineers build integrations.
Hotel staff want a guest-question assistant prototype, and a simple prompt flow tested in the Playground shows tone and answers before any booking systems connect.

cards.title: Langflow overview
cards.definition: Build agents and AI workflows visually, then serve the same flow as an API, MCP tool or A2A agent.
points: A flow is a graph of components drawn on a canvas and stored as JSON.
The flow tested in the Playground is the flow the API serves.
Visual building speeds iteration but does not remove the need to review what the flow does.
useCases: Workshop demo to production — a developer wires a support-triage flow on the canvas, tests it in the Playground, then calls the same flow from the helpdesk backend over its API.
Prompt review before launch — a lead opens the canvas of a drafted agent to check each component's prompt and tool wiring before the flow is exposed to other teams.

industries.problem: Agents need a listing-question assistant built quickly with the web team, and one tested flow must serve the site without a rebuild in code.
Admissions staff without deep coding skills must prototype an applicant FAQ agent, with engineers still reviewing what it does before students use it.

cards.title: Typed data: Message, JSON and Table
cards.definition: Ports carry typed data, and an output connects only to an input that accepts the same type.
points: Message carries chat text plus sender, session ID and files.
JSON (named Data before 1.9) is a structured record; Table (named DataFrame before 1.9) holds rows.
Parser and type-conversion components bridge types when a flow mixes them.
useCases: Turning search results into an answer — Web Search returns a Table of results; a Parser formats the rows into text, which feeds a Prompt Template whose output becomes the Message the model answers.

Turning an AI prototype into an API in an afternoon — A RAG pipeline or agent built and tested on the canvas is called from the app over its run endpoint, with no orchestration code written for the join.

industries.problem: A policy assistant over company documents is needed in days, and a visual RAG flow served as an API removes the rewrite between prototype and integration.
Teams want their internal workflows callable from AI assistants, and publishing flows as MCP tools avoids writing a separate server for each.

parts: Typed data: Message, JSON and Table

cards.title: Installation options
cards.definition: Choose Langflow Desktop, the Python package or the Docker image depending on who runs it and where.
points: Langflow Desktop is the quickest single-user install on Windows and macOS.
The `langflow` Python package needs Python 3.10–3.14 and is installed with `uv pip install langflow`.
Official Docker images disable auto-login, so they need a superuser password.
useCases: Matching the install to the job — A data scientist uses Desktop to prototype, the platform team runs the Docker image on Kubernetes for the shared instance, and CI uses the Python package with LFX to run flows headlessly.

Turning an AI prototype into an API in an afternoon — A RAG pipeline or agent built and tested on the canvas is called from the app over its run endpoint, with no orchestration code written for the join.

industries.problem: A policy assistant over company documents is needed in days, and a visual RAG flow served as an API removes the rewrite between prototype and integration.
Teams want their internal workflows callable from AI assistants, and publishing flows as MCP tools avoids writing a separate server for each.

cards.title: router.push
cards.definition: Programmatically navigate to a route from a Client Component while adding a new browser-history entry.
points: Use the hook when navigation must be triggered by component logic rather than a declarative link.
Its signature takes a destination string and an optional navigation-options object.
The route changes through client-side navigation instead of requiring a full document reload.
useCases: Navigate after an event — A button submits a form and then opens the newly created record.
Update client-driven URL state — A filter updates the URL query string without a full page reload.

industries.problem: Checkout steps need client-side validation before moving on, while Back must return to the previous step's route.
After a patient confirms a time slot, the app must open the booking confirmation without a full reload losing form state.

cards.title: Cache Components
cards.definition: Cache Components enables component- and function-level caching with use cache.
points: The feature lets you cache at component or function granularity instead of treating only an entire route as the caching unit.
Apply use cache to a route, component, or function to cache its returned work.
A file-level directive covers every export, while an inline directive limits caching to one function or component.
useCases: Cache stable server work — Reuse stable database reads or rendered UI between requests.
Stream dynamic sections — Keep a route responsive while request-specific content resolves.

industries.problem: Category pages mix a shared product grid with a per-user cart badge, and caching the grid alone avoids recomputing it per visit.
Article pages combine stable body content with a live comment count, so only the costly article render is reused between readers.

cards.title: Proxy
cards.definition: Next.js 16 calls the former Middleware convention Proxy.
points: In Next.js 16, the former Middleware convention is renamed Proxy; the underlying capability remains available.
Proxy is suitable for decisions that must happen before the route finishes processing.
A Proxy function can redirect, rewrite, change headers, or produce a response without rendering the target route.
useCases: Programmatic redirects — A request contains an expired or legacy URL that should move to a new route.
Conditional rewrites — Different incoming requests should reach different pages based on an experiment or request property.

industries.problem: Blocks unauthenticated checkout and account requests early so protected order pages never render for signed-out visitors.
Sends readers to a regional edition by language header, so the right localized site loads without a client-side flash.

cards.title: useSelectedLayoutSegment in tabs
cards.definition: useSelectedLayoutSegment is a Client Component hook for reading the active route segment immediately below a layout.
points: Use it inside a Client Component to inspect the child route directly beneath the layout that invokes it.
A tab bar can compare each tab's segment name with the hook result to choose the active styling.
Pass a parallel-route key when the tab state belongs to a named slot rather than the default route.
useCases: Highlight the active dashboard tab — A shared dashboard layout contains links for overview, reports, and settings pages.
Track a slot-specific tab state — A named parallel-route slot has independently navigable child pages.

industries.problem: Customers lose their place in a dashboard when the tab bar doesn't show which report section is open beneath the shared layout.
A patient record page needs a side-panel tab to stay correct when its named slot changes independently of the main chart view.

cards.title: useReportWebVitals analytics
cards.definition: Use `useReportWebVitals` in a Client Component to receive Core Web Vitals and send metric data to an analytics endpoint.
points: Use the hook to report Core Web Vitals and connect those measurements to an analytics service.
The supplied callback receives metrics that are available when the callback is processed.
The callback argument is a metric object containing several properties for identification and measurement.
useCases: Custom performance analytics — Send serialized metric objects to a server endpoint for storage and dashboarding.
Soft-navigation attribution — Associate delayed soft-navigation measurements with the navigation that produced them.

industries.problem: Editors see slow article pages in lab tests but lack field data showing which templates hurt LCP for real readers.
Search-results pages feel sluggish on mobile, and teams need per-route INP data from real sessions to find the interactions causing it.

cards.title: Streaming with Suspense
cards.definition: Use Suspense boundaries to send a route’s ready shell and fallback first, then stream slower server-rendered regions as they resolve.
points: Treat every Suspense boundary as a separate delivery point for progressive rendering.
Sibling boundaries can reveal their completed UI at different times rather than waiting for one shared result.
Add loading.tsx beside a page when route-level streaming and an automatic fallback are sufficient.
useCases: Show the page shell before slow data — A route has a slow data request but includes headings, navigation, or controls that can render immediately.
Reveal independent widgets progressively — Several dashboard widgets have different response times.

industries.problem: Flight search pages stay blank while slow airline fare lookups finish, so streaming shows the form and results as each source answers.
Account overview pages wait on slow ledger and portfolio queries, so streaming shows balances first and heavier statements as they resolve.

cards.title: useSelectedLayoutSegments and route groups
cards.definition: A Client Component hook that reads active route segments below the calling layout.
points: Use it in a Client Component to inspect active segments beneath the calling layout.
The returned array contains the active child segments one level below the layout.
If the layout has no active child segment, the hook returns an empty array.
useCases: Breadcrumbs — A layout needs to show the current nested path without exposing filesystem-only grouping.
Section labels — A parent layout changes a section heading or navigation state based on its active descendants.

industries.problem: Docs layouts must highlight the open section from the URL even when route groups organize files without changing the path.
Account area layouts must show which nested section is open, such as cards or statements, without parsing the pathname by hand.

cards.title: cacheLife and cacheTag
cards.definition: Use cacheLife to define how long cached data remains valid and cacheTag to group cached entries for on-demand invalidation.
points: Use cacheLife to choose how long a cached function or component remains valid before time-based revalidation.
Pass a named profile such as hours, or provide a custom cache-life configuration when the built-in profiles do not fit.
Attach one or more meaningful tags to cached data so a later mutation or administrative action can invalidate related entries.
useCases: Time-based freshness — Data with a predictable refresh interval, such as hourly metrics.
Mutation-driven invalidation — A product or CMS record that must be refreshed after an edit.

industries.problem: Cached carrier status pages stay fresh for minutes, and a delay webhook expires only the affected shipment's tag.
Listing pages are cached, but a price change or sale must clear that listing and its search results quickly.

cards.title: useSelectedLayoutSegment
cards.definition: A Client Component hook that reads the active route segment immediately below the layout containing it.
points: Import it from next/navigation and use it only in a Client Component.
The returned segment is relative to the containing layout, not necessarily the first segment of the full URL.
Use it to derive active styling for tabs or links controlled by child routes.
useCases: Mark the current tab active — A parent layout contains tabs for child routes such as overview and settings.
Inspect a slot's selected child — A layout renders navigation for a named parallel route.

industries.problem: Project workspaces with board, timeline, and files views need the current view highlighted without matching full URL strings.
Account pages nested under a customer ID need the right sub-section marked, such as cards or statements, whatever the ID prefix is.

cards.title: router.replace
cards.definition: `router.replace` performs client-side navigation to a route without adding a new browser-history entry.
points: The destination replaces the current history position instead of creating another Back-button step.
Use the hook when navigation must be triggered by component logic, such as a submit handler or button event.
Its signature takes a destination string and an options object for scroll behavior and transition types.
useCases: Update query parameters as users submit or change filters without creating a Back-button entry for every change. — Search and filtering
Replace a temporary or obsolete route after completing an action so users do not return to it with Back. — Redirect after an intermediate step

industries.problem: After a transfer is confirmed, Back should not reopen a one-time review page that could prompt a duplicate submission.
Once a seat hold expires, the countdown route is swapped for a refreshed seat map so Back does not revive a dead reservation.

cards.title: Intercepting routes
cards.definition: Intercepting routes render a destination inside the current layout, preserving the user's context for patterns such as photo modals.
points: They render a destination from elsewhere in the app without leaving the current layout context.
A photo detail view can appear as a modal over a feed while the feed remains underneath.
Client navigation can overlay the intercepted destination while masking the browser URL with the originating route.
useCases: Photo preview modal — A user selects a photo from a feed.
Context-preserving details — A list item opens a detail view without losing the list context.

industries.problem: Shoppers lose scroll position and filters in a product grid when opening an item, but each product still needs a shareable URL.
Buyers browsing map-based listings lose their search view when opening a property, yet each listing needs its own linkable page.

cards.title: useOffline
cards.definition: useOffline returns whether a Next.js app is currently offline.
points: The hook’s result is a boolean representing the app’s current offline state.
useOffline only reports status; the configuration option also enables detection and request retry behavior.
Import the hook from next/offline.
useCases: Offline banner — Show an always-visible indicator when connectivity is lost.
Offline-aware loading UI — Tell users why a pending route or request has not completed.

industries.problem: Technicians in basements or rural sites need to know when job updates cannot sync, so they don't assume a report was sent.
Drivers passing through tunnels need a clear offline signal so a stalled trip request is not mistaken for an app crash.

cards.title: router.refresh
cards.definition: router.refresh() requests a fresh server render of the current route, refetching route data and re-rendering Server Components.
points: The method targets the currently displayed route; it does not require a destination URL.
It initiates a server request, repeats data requests, and renders the route's Server Components again.
The new server-rendered payload is merged into the existing client UI rather than replacing unaffected client state.
useCases: Reflect a completed mutation — A user submits or completes an operation and the current route should display its latest server-rendered values.
Re-evaluate request-time data — The response depends on request-time cookies or headers and the current UI should be rerun without navigation.

industries.problem: After a teammate-triggered status change is saved, the board's server-rendered counts must update without resetting open drawers or drag state.
After a user switches the active account via a cookie, the server-rendered balances must rerun without a full navigation clearing the open transfer form.

cards.title: Nested layouts
cards.definition: Nested layouts let you share UI across a route subtree.
points: Use `layout.tsx` for interface elements shared by several pages rather than duplicating them in each page.
The directory structure automatically creates the parent-child layout relationship.
A parent layout renders its nested layout or page by placing `children` in its JSX.
useCases: Application shell — A site-wide shell should surround every App Router page.
Section navigation — Several dashboard pages need the same navigation and controls.

industries.problem: Lesson pages under a course need the same outline sidebar and progress bar without each page re-implementing them.
Listing pages under an agency need shared branding and a contact panel, with search and detail views nested inside one frame.

cards.title: Static and dynamic rendering
cards.definition: Static rendering builds or revalidates a page ahead of requests and serves its cached result.
points: Static rendering performs data fetching and rendering during the build, or later when cached data is revalidated.
Subsequent visitors receive the cached rendered result rather than triggering rendering for every request.
Use static rendering for pages whose content is identical or broadly shareable between users.
useCases: Shared catalog content — A blog post or product page is shared across users and can be generated before requests.
Personalized dashboards — A dashboard displays user-specific information or data that must be current at request time.

industries.problem: Course landing pages get enrollment-day traffic spikes, and rendering identical content per visit wastes server work.
Public notices must load fast under traffic spikes, while permit status lookups need current per-applicant data.

cards.title: useRouter back and forward
cards.definition: Use the App Router’s `useRouter` hook in a Client Component to traverse existing browser history.
points: Import `useRouter` from `next/navigation` when a Client Component needs imperative route control.
Call `router.back()` to move one entry toward the beginning of browser history.
Call `router.forward()` to move one entry toward the end of browser history.
useCases: Close a history-backed view — A modal or detail view was opened from another route and should close by returning to the prior history entry.
Build history controls — A custom navigation toolbar should reproduce browser-style backward and forward movement.

industries.problem: Reviewers open a case document from a search results list and need a Close button that returns them to the exact result page.
Learners stepping through lesson pages need in-player previous and next controls that follow the history they already walked through.

cards.title: NextRequest
cards.definition: Extends Request with `cookies`, `nextUrl` and geo/IP where the platform provides it.
points: `req.nextUrl` is a URL object with `pathname` and `searchParams`, plus Next.js extras like `basePath`.
`req.cookies.get/has/set/delete` read and change request cookies.
It is accepted wherever a `Request` is, so you can type Route Handler arguments with it.
useCases: Cookie-based A/B bucketing — A Route Handler reads req.cookies.get('variant'), assigns one if missing, and returns the choice so later requests stay in the same bucket.
Webhook path and query parsing — A Route Handler typed with NextRequest reads req.nextUrl.searchParams to pick the tenant and event type from a callback URL.

industries.problem: Course pages must remember a learner's chosen language from a cookie so the API returns the right subtitles without a login.
A parcel-tracking endpoint must read the tracking ID and carrier from the URL query to return the right shipment status.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: cacheTag
cards.definition: Tags a cached entry so `revalidateTag` can invalidate it later.
points: Call it inside a `'use cache'` scope; one entry can carry several tags.
Tag by entity — `cacheTag('products', `product-${id}`)` — so you can clear one item or all of them.
Tags are invalidated with `updateTag` or `revalidateTag`.
useCases: Per-product cache tags — A product detail component tags its cached render with `product-${id}`, so editing one SKU clears only that page's cached entry.
Group and item tags together — A cached category listing carries both a 'products' tag and per-item tags, so a bulk price import can clear every cached product at once.

industries.problem: Sellers edit single listings often, and tagging each cached listing by ID refreshes just that one without flushing the whole catalog.
A corrected article must update on its page and in section lists, so tags like author or section let one invalidation reach every cached view.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: "use client"
cards.definition: Marks the module and its imports as the client boundary.
points: It goes at the very top of the file, above imports; every module that file imports becomes client code too.
Props crossing into a Client Component must be serializable — functions cannot be passed, except Server Functions.
Push it down to the leaf that needs state or browser APIs, so the parent layout and its data stay on the server.
useCases: Interactive leaf in a server page — Only a quantity stepper with useState is marked as a client file, so the surrounding product page and its data fetch stay on the server.
Wrap a browser-only widget — A map or chart library that touches window gets a thin client wrapper, so the server layout can render it without importing the library itself.

industries.problem: Menu pages need a working add-to-basket control, but marking the whole page client-side would ship restaurant data fetching to the browser.
A shipment tracking page needs a browser-only map component, and isolating it keeps the heavy map code out of the server-rendered status table.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: sitemap.js
cards.definition: Returns sitemap entries; `generateSitemaps` splits very large sites into several files.
points: Return an array of `{ url, lastModified, changeFrequency, priority }`, typed as `MetadataRoute.Sitemap`.
It is a special Route Handler and is cached by default unless it uses request-time APIs.
One sitemap can hold at most 50,000 URLs — split larger sites with `generateSitemaps`.
useCases: Product URL feed — A catalog route reads active product slugs from a database and returns each with its lastModified date so crawlers find new items.
Sharded sitemap for a large marketplace — generateSitemaps returns id values so each file lists up to 50,000 listing URLs, split by id range.

industries.problem: Millions of listing URLs change daily, so crawlers miss new items unless split sitemap files list them with fresh lastModified dates.
New articles must be discoverable by search engines within minutes, so the sitemap must list recent stories with accurate modification times.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: "use cache: private"
cards.definition: Caches a function that reads `cookies()`, `headers()` or `searchParams` — in the browser's memory only, never on the server.
points: Use it only when moving `cookies()` or `headers()` outside the cached function and passing values in is not practical.
The function still runs on every server render; what is saved is repeat work during client navigation and prefetch.
Custom cache handlers cannot be used with it, and the `stale` time must be at least 30 seconds for per-link prefetching to work.
useCases: Locale-aware price list — A helper reads the Accept-Language header and a currency cookie deep in shared code, and caching its result in the browser avoids recomputing it when users move between product pages.

Prefetched account sidebar — A nav component reads a session cookie to build the user's workspace list, so hovering links reuses the in-memory result instead of repeating the lookup on each client navigation.

industries.problem: Delivery-slot and substitution lookups depend on a postcode cookie, and repeating them on every aisle navigation slows browsing without sharing data between shoppers.
Ticket queue pages read the agent's session cookie for team filters, and switching between queues should reuse results without storing private data on a shared server cache.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: useReportWebVitals placement
cards.definition: Mount it once in a small client component near the root, not in every page that wants metrics.
points: A dedicated client component near the root mounts it once.
The docs call a separate component the most performant approach.
Mounting it per page multiplies every metric by the number of listeners.
useCases: Composing navigation logic once — Read-the-query-then-replace-it logic repeated across pages becomes one Hook, so the debounce and the history behaviour match everywhere.

Reacting to the URL from a component — Filters, tabs and pagination live in the address bar so they survive a reload and can be shared as a link; these Hooks are how a component reads and changes that.

industries.problem: Product and checkout pages each had their own reporter, so analytics showed inflated LCP counts and skewed per-template averages.
Article, section and live-blog templates must feed one Web Vitals pipeline without each template adding its own listener and duplicate events.

cards.title: images
cards.definition: Remote patterns, device sizes, formats and the loader.
points: `remotePatterns` lists allowed hosts with protocol, hostname and optional path.
`formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp']` turns on AVIF for smaller files.
`unoptimized: true` serves originals — needed for `output: 'export'` without a loader.
useCases: Allow-list a CMS image host — A product page renders photos from a headless CMS CDN, so `remotePatterns` permits only that hostname and path prefix and rejects other URLs.
Static export without a loader — A marketing site built with `output: 'export'` sets `unoptimized: true` since no server exists to resize images on request.

industries.problem: Listing photos come from agency-uploaded buckets, so unrestricted proxying is risky; allow-listing hosts keeps the optimizer from fetching arbitrary URLs.
Hotel hero images are huge on mobile networks, and enabling AVIF output shrinks them so search results load faster for travelers on cellular data.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: generateImageMetadata
cards.definition: Generates several images from one file convention, each with its own metadata.
points: Return an array of `{ id, alt, size, contentType }`, one per image.
The image function receives each `id` to render the matching variant.
Useful for several icon sizes or several Open Graph images from one file.
useCases: Multi-size app icons — One icon.tsx exports generateImageMetadata returning 16, 32 and 180px entries, and the image function draws each size from its id.
Per-slide Open Graph images — A product page's opengraph-image file returns one entry per gallery photo so each shared link can show a different preview.

industries.problem: A news site's PWA needs several icon sizes for home screens and tabs without keeping a hand-maintained folder of exported PNGs.
A listing shared in chat should preview with different property photos, rendered from one file instead of one route per image.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: catchError
cards.definition: Creates an error-boundary component in code — the programmatic form of `error.js` that lets `redirect()` and `notFound()` pass through.
points: The fallback receives your props plus `{ error, retry }` (or `reset` outside the App Router).
`retry()` re-renders inside a Transition, keeping Client Component state outside the boundary.
The error state clears automatically on client navigation to another route.
useCases: Widget-level fallback with retry — A dashboard revenue chart that throws on a failed fetch shows its own error card with a Retry button, while the sidebar and filters keep their state.
Reusable boundary that ignores redirects — A shared wrapper around a data-loading panel shows a custom error UI but lets redirect() to sign-in and notFound() reach the router.

industries.problem: A failing portfolio widget must show a retry card without wiping the transfer form state sitting beside it on the page.
One ticket-history panel throwing on a flaky API should not blank the open reply draft or force a full page reload.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: <Image>
cards.definition: Automatic sizing, lazy loading, responsive `srcset` and format negotiation.
points: Remote images need their host allowed in `images.remotePatterns`, or the optimizer refuses them.
Use `sizes` with `fill` or responsive layouts — without it the browser may download the largest variant.
Mark the hero image with `preload` (formerly `priority`) so the Largest Contentful Paint image is not lazy-loaded.
useCases: Hero banner preload — A landing page's full-width banner is the Largest Contentful Paint element, so `preload` stops it from being lazy-loaded below the fold logic.
Fill-mode card grid — Article cards use `fill` inside aspect-ratio boxes with `sizes="(min-width: 768px) 33vw, 100vw"` so phones don't fetch the widest variant.

industries.problem: Product photos with unknown dimensions shift the page as they load, so reserved width and height keep the aisle grid stable.
Editors upload huge lead photos, and responsive variants plus lazy loading keep long article pages light for readers on mobile.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: Parallel routes
cards.definition: `@slot` folders render several pages into one layout at the same time.
points: Each `@slot` arrives as a prop on the parent layout, next to `children`.
Slots navigate independently, each with its own `loading.js` and `error.js`.
Every slot needs a `default.js` to stay visible after a refresh.
useCases: Dashboard with independent panels — A layout renders @analytics and @activity beside children, so each panel streams with its own loading.js and a failing feed shows only its own error.js.
Slot fallback after hard refresh — A tabbed @sidebar slot holds a deep route, and default.js keeps the layout from returning a 404 when a user reloads on that URL.

industries.problem: Agents need a ticket thread, customer profile and macro suggestions on screen at once, each loading and failing separately without blanking the others.
A trading screen shows the order form, a live watchlist and positions together, and one slow or failing feed must not block the others.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: forbidden.js
cards.definition: The UI for `forbidden()` — a 403, distinct from a 404.
points: Enable it with `experimental: { authInterrupts: true }` in next.config.
Use it for a signed-in user who lacks permission; signed-out users belong to `unauthorized.js`.
The page responds with HTTP 403, so clients and crawlers can tell it apart from a missing page.
useCases: Admin-only settings page — A signed-in member opens /settings/billing without the owner role, and forbidden() renders a 403 page instead of the billing form.
Per-resource access check — A document route loads the file, sees the user isn't on its sharing list, and calls forbidden() so a 403 is returned, not a 404.

industries.problem: Associates must see a clear 'no access' page for case files under an ethical wall, not a misleading 'not found' or a leaked document.
Employees who open another team's payroll or review pages need a 403 response, so access errors are distinguishable from broken links in logs.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: generateStaticParams
cards.definition: Enumerates the dynamic params to prerender at build time.
points: Return an array of param objects, e.g. `[{ slug: 'a' }, { slug: 'b' }]`.
Returning a partial list prerenders the popular pages and leaves the rest to render on demand.
Under Cache Components at least one param is required so the route can be validated at build.
useCases: Prerender top blog posts — generateStaticParams returns slugs for the 200 most-read posts, so those pages ship as static HTML and the long tail renders on first request.
Build-time locale routes — A [lang]/docs/[slug] route returns each language and slug pair from the docs folder, so every translated page is generated during the build.

industries.problem: Thousands of recipe pages exist, but only popular ones need prebuilding, so builds stay short while rarely viewed recipes render on demand.
Versioned API reference pages need one static page per release and endpoint, and listing those params at build avoids slow runtime rendering.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: Forms and progressive enhancement
cards.definition: Submit mutations from server-rendered forms that remain useful before client JavaScript loads.
points: A form whose action is a server function submits before the JavaScript bundle loads, and upgrades silently once it does.
The action receives FormData, so field names in the markup are the contract.
Keeping validation in the action rather than in the client means the rule holds even when the request does not come from your form.
useCases: A sign-up that works on a bad connection — On a slow phone the form still posts and responds; the client bundle improves the experience rather than being required for it.
Writing data without a separate API layer — A form posts to a server function and the affected pages refresh, instead of a hand-written endpoint plus client fetch plus manual cache invalidation.

industries.problem: Residents on old phones or locked-down browsers must still submit service requests, so forms work as plain posts without relying on client scripts.
Appointment request forms must validate on the server since patients, scripts or integrations may post data that never passed the page's client-side checks.

cards.title: next lint
cards.definition: Removed in Next.js 16.
points: Install `eslint` and `eslint-config-next`, then extend `next/core-web-vitals` in `eslint.config.mjs`.
Add `"lint": "eslint ."` to package.json scripts.
A codemod migrates projects: `npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .`.
useCases: Migrate a legacy lint script — A repo whose package.json runs `next lint` after upgrading to 16 swaps it for `eslint .` and adds an `eslint.config.mjs` extending `next/core-web-vitals`.
Run the codemod across a monorepo — A team runs `npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .` in each app folder to rewrite lint scripts instead of editing dozens of files by hand.

industries.problem: A dealer-portal CI pipeline fails after the Next.js 16 upgrade because its lint step still calls the removed `next lint` command.
Many small course-site repos share a stale lint script, so a codemod keeps their ESLint setup consistent after the framework upgrade.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: app icons
cards.definition: `favicon`, `icon` and `apple-icon` conventions, including generated variants.
points: Place `icon.png` or `apple-icon.png` in `app/` and the `<link>` tags are generated for you.
`favicon.ico` only works at the top level of `app/`.
`icon.tsx` can generate an icon with `ImageResponse`, such as a letter or status badge.
useCases: Status badge favicon — An icon.tsx draws a colored dot with ImageResponse so the browser tab shows whether a staging or production build is open.
Brand letter fallback — A multi-tenant app's icon.tsx renders the first letter of the workspace name on a colored square, avoiding a hand-exported PNG per tenant.

industries.problem: Engineers keep many dashboard tabs open, and a distinct generated icon per environment helps avoid acting on production by mistake.
Clinic portals saved to iPhone home screens need a clear apple-icon so staff recognize the app without a custom icon pipeline.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: NextResponse
cards.definition: Extends Response with `redirect`, `rewrite`, `next` and cookie helpers, mainly for proxy.js.
points: `NextResponse.next()` continues the request — used in proxy to add headers.
`NextResponse.rewrite(url)` serves another path while keeping the URL in the address bar.
`NextResponse.json(data, { status })` is a shortcut for JSON responses in Route Handlers.
useCases: Locale rewrite in proxy — A proxy reads the Accept-Language header and calls NextResponse.rewrite to serve /fr/pricing while the visitor's address bar still shows /pricing.
Session cookie refresh — A proxy checks an expiring session cookie, calls NextResponse.next(), and sets a renewed cookie on that response so pages see a fresh login.

industries.problem: Each customer's subdomain must show its own tenant pages, and rewriting to an internal path avoids duplicating routes per tenant.
Patients with expired sessions must be redirected to sign-in before any record page renders, with a return path kept in the redirect URL.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: page.js
cards.definition: Makes a route segment publicly routable and renders its UI.
points: `params` and `searchParams` are promises in Next.js 16 — `const { id } = await params`.
A page is a Server Component by default, so it can `await` the database directly.
`PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>` gives fully typed props generated from your route tree.
useCases: Typed blog post route — A /blog/[slug] page awaits params, loads the post straight from the database as a Server Component, and uses PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'> so slug typing never drifts from the folder.
Filterable results page — A /search page awaits searchParams to read q and page, queries the database for that slice, and renders results on the server without client fetching.

industries.problem: Each job opening needs its own public URL showing live role data, without building a separate API and client fetch for every posting page.
Clinic profile pages need typed route ids and URL filters like specialty or date, so bad params don't reach appointment queries.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: taint
cards.definition: Enables React's taint APIs, so a flagged object or value cannot cross to the client.
points: `experimental.taint: true` enables React's `taintObjectReference` and `taintUniqueValue`.
A tainted value throws if it is passed to a Client Component.
It is a safety net, not a replacement for returning only the fields the UI needs.
useCases: Taint a loaded user record — A Server Component calls taintObjectReference on the full account row so passing it whole to a Client Component profile form throws instead of leaking fields.
Taint an API secret string — A server module calls taintUniqueValue on a payment provider key read from env, so any component that forwards that exact string to the browser fails.

industries.problem: Patient records fetched on the server hold diagnosis and insurance fields, and one careless prop must not ship the whole record to the browser.
Server code handles API tokens and customer payment references, and tainting them stops a refactor from passing them into client components.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: reactStrictMode
cards.definition: Double-invokes render in development to surface impure components.
points: It is on by default in the App Router.
Effects run, clean up and run again in development to catch missing cleanup.
It has no effect in production builds.
useCases: Catch missing effect cleanup — A chat widget opens a WebSocket in useEffect, and the dev-only mount, unmount, remount cycle shows duplicate connections when the close call is missing.
Expose render-time mutation — A cart summary component pushes items into a module-level array during render, and double rendering makes totals double in development so the impurity is caught.

industries.problem: A live quotes panel that leaks subscriptions on unmount shows duplicate ticks in development, so the missing cleanup is found before release.
Patient intake forms that mutate shared state while rendering show inconsistent values in development, before they cause wrong data in clinic workflows.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: manifest.js
cards.definition: Generates the web app manifest for installable PWAs.
points: Return a `MetadataRoute.Manifest` with `name`, `start_url`, `display` and `icons`.
Next.js serves it at `/manifest.webmanifest` and links it from every page.
Combined with a service worker it makes the app installable on phones and desktops.
useCases: Installable field-service app — manifest.ts returns name, start_url '/jobs', display 'standalone' and icons so technicians can add the job list to their phone home screen.
Environment-specific install name — manifest.ts reads an env variable to return 'Admin (Staging)' versus 'Admin', so installed copies of each build are easy to tell apart.

industries.problem: Staff want the kitchen order screen to open full-screen from a tablet icon, not a browser tab where they can wander off.
Technicians in low-signal areas need an installable job app that launches straight to today's work list from the home screen.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: cacheLife
cards.definition: Sets the stale, revalidate and expire profile for a `'use cache'` boundary.
points: Built-in profiles: `'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'` and `'max'`.
`stale` is how long the client uses it without asking, `revalidate` when the server refreshes it in the background, `expire` when it must be refetched.
Define your own named profiles in next.config's `cacheLife` key.
useCases: Short-lived stock badge — A cached inventory component calls cacheLife('seconds') so product pages show near-live availability without querying the warehouse API on every request.
Custom editorial profile — next.config defines a 'headlines' cacheLife with its own stale, revalidate and expire, so every cached homepage feed component shares one tuned policy.

industries.problem: Seat availability changes by the minute during on-sales, so a seconds-level cache lifetime avoids hammering the inventory service while staying near-current.
Forecast pages need hourly refreshes but archives rarely change, so separate cacheLife profiles avoid recomputing old data while keeping current outlooks fresh.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: connection
cards.definition: Marks the point where rendering must wait for a real request, opting out of prerendering.
points: Use it before `Math.random()`, `new Date()` or a synchronous database query that must run per request.
Unlike `io()`, it also blocks prefetches until a real navigation reaches the server.
With `cookies()` or `headers()` already in use, it is not needed — they are request signals themselves.
useCases: Per-request nonce token — A page generates a random CSP nonce with Math.random() in a server component, so connection() ensures each response gets a fresh value, not a prerendered one.
Live server clock banner — A status page prints new Date() for the render time, and connection() keeps it from being frozen at build while prefetches skip it until a real visit.

industries.problem: Seat-hold countdowns use the current time and a synchronous lookup, so they must be computed per visitor and never baked into a prerender.
Daily-challenge pages pick a random seed per visit, and prerendering would show every player the same seed fixed at build time.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: turbopackChunking
cards.definition: Tunes how modules are grouped into chunks.
points: It tunes the production JavaScript chunker's size thresholds.
It is experimental and most apps should keep the defaults.
Measure bundle output before and after changing it.
useCases: Splitting an oversized vendor chunk — A dashboard's production build emits one huge shared chunk from charting and date libraries, so a team raises or lowers chunker size thresholds and compares output.

Taming request waterfalls from tiny chunks — A route imports dozens of small modules that become many small files, so tuning chunk thresholds is tried and the build's chunk list is diffed before and after.

industries.problem: Checkout pages load too many small script files on slow mobile links, so engineers test chunk size thresholds against measured bundle output.
A web player app ships a heavy shared chunk to every page, and threshold tuning is checked against build output to cut first-load JavaScript.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: next/image
cards.definition: Resize, optimize and serve responsive images with safe remote source configuration.
points: Remote sources must be allow-listed in config, which stops the optimizer being used as an open proxy.
`priority` preloads the image the reader sees first; using it on several images removes the benefit.
`fill` needs a positioned parent, and forgetting that is why an image sometimes collapses to nothing.
useCases: A product gallery on a slow connection — Each thumbnail arrives at the size that device needs rather than a 3MB original scaled down in the browser.
Passing Core Web Vitals on real phones — Images, fonts and scripts are the usual cause of a slow page; the tooling here is what keeps layout shift and main-thread work down.

industries.problem: Listing pages show dozens of large agent-uploaded photos, and serving each at device size keeps search results fast on mobile.
Article lead images must load first and stay inside a sized box, so readers don't see text jump as photos from the CMS arrive.

cards.title: permanentRedirect
cards.definition: The 308 counterpart, for URLs that have moved for good.
points: It returns 308, which tells browsers and search engines to update their links.
Use it when a URL has moved for good, such as a renamed slug.
For many fixed redirects, prefer `redirects` in next.config, which runs before rendering.
useCases: Renamed blog slug — A post editor changes /blog/old-title to /blog/new-title, and the old route calls permanentRedirect so search engines transfer ranking to the new URL.
Username change profile URL — A /u/[handle] page finds the handle in a rename table and calls permanentRedirect to the current handle so old shared links keep working.

industries.problem: Renamed product slugs break bookmarks and lose search ranking unless old URLs permanently point to the new ones.
Reorganized article paths leave years of inbound links stale, so old URLs must signal a permanent move to crawlers.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: mdx-components.js
cards.definition: Maps MDX elements to your components, required by `@next/mdx`.
points: It sits at the project root and exports `useMDXComponents`, which `@next/mdx` requires in the App Router.
Mapping `h1` or `a` here styles every MDX page at once, without imports in each file.
Add `md`/`mdx` to `pageExtensions` so `.mdx` files can be pages.
useCases: Branded headings and links — mdx-components.js maps h1 and a to design-system components so every .mdx docs page gets the same typography and link behavior without imports.
Custom callout in MDX — useMDXComponents exposes a Callout component so writers can drop <Callout> into any .mdx page without a per-file import statement.

industries.problem: Hundreds of MDX guides must share code block, heading anchor and link styling, and one mapping file avoids editing each page.
Writers publish MDX case studies that must use approved brand components, so mapping elements centrally keeps layouts consistent without developer help.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: after
cards.definition: Schedules work to run after the response is sent — logging and analytics without delaying the user.
points: It runs after the response finishes streaming, even when the response failed or redirected.
Inside `after` you can still read `cookies()` and `headers()` in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
It is not a durable queue — use a job system for work that must survive a crash.
useCases: Audit log after checkout — A checkout Server Function returns the order confirmation, then `after` writes the audit row and sends the analytics event so the buyer never waits on them.
Request-scoped logging in a Route Handler — An API route calls `after` to read `headers()` for the request ID and user agent, then flushes structured logs once the response has been sent.

industries.problem: Purchase confirmations should appear instantly, while conversion tracking and inventory sync events are sent once the response is already on its way.
Play and search endpoints must reply fast, while usage metrics and recommendation signals are recorded after the response without adding latency.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: "use cache: remote"
cards.definition: Caches into the shared remote cache handler rather than only in memory.
points: The default `use cache` store is in-memory per instance — evicted under pressure and lost on restart; remote is durable and shared.
Every lookup now costs a network round trip, so it only pays off for slow or rate-limited upstream calls.
Avoid it for keys that are unique per request (search filters, user ids) — the hit rate will be near zero.
useCases: Cache a rate-limited pricing API — A product page calls a vendor exchange-rate endpoint capped per minute, so 'use cache: remote' shares one result across all serverless instances.
Survive deploy restarts — An expensive report-aggregation function stays cached in the shared handler, so a new instance after a cold start doesn't recompute it.

industries.problem: Airline fare lookups are slow and quota-limited, so a shared remote cache stops every serverless instance from calling the supplier separately.
Daily market-summary calls to a metered data vendor must survive restarts and scale-out, or each fresh instance burns paid request quota.

parts: Next.js 16+ APIs — Directives, Functions, Hooks & Config

cards.title: Components & JSX
cards.definition: React components are JavaScript functions that return JSX, a stricter HTML-like syntax for describing UI.
points: Treat each independently defined UI piece as a component, then combine those pieces to form the application.
The core component model is a JavaScript function whose returned result includes markup-like JSX.
JSX resembles HTML but follows stricter syntax rules, so familiar HTML may need small adjustments.
useCases: Reusable interface pieces — Create reusable UI elements such as buttons, cards, or navigation sections.
Markup with JavaScript — Keep rendering logic and displayed content together in a component file.

industries.problem: Flight search results repeat the same fare card layout, so one component keeps hundreds of itinerary listings consistent and easy to update.
Campaign pages mix donation forms, progress bars and story sections, and JSX lets small teams assemble and revise them as separate pieces.

cards.title: useActionState
cards.definition: Pair an Action with its latest result and pending flag.
points: It connects an Action to state, making the Action's latest result available to rendering code.
Initialize it during component rendering at the top level, rather than in event-driven or conditional code.
The reducer gets its prior result first, then the payload supplied to the returned dispatch function.
useCases: Render the latest submission result — A form needs to display server or validation feedback after each submission.
Disable controls while an Action is pending — A submit control should reflect asynchronous work.

industries.problem: A transfer form must show the bank's rejection reason and block resubmission while the payment request is still in flight.
A ticket reply form must show send failures or confirmation on the same screen, so agents know whether a message went out.

cards.title: useLayoutEffect
cards.definition: Use useLayoutEffect for layout measurement or visual corrections that must happen before the browser paints.
points: It is designed for effects whose timing must precede the next browser paint.
A typical use is reading an element's geometry before displaying a layout-dependent result.
Return cleanup code when the effect creates subscriptions, listeners, or other resources that need removal.
useCases: Measure and position an overlay — A tooltip or popover must be positioned from its measured dimensions before the first visible paint.
Synchronize layout-dependent state — A component needs to read an element's bounding rectangle and update state before the user sees an intermediate layout.

industries.problem: Chart labels and callouts need measured text sizes to avoid overlap, without a visible jump after the first paint.
Editors' floating formatting toolbars must sit beside the selected text immediately, without flashing in the wrong spot.

cards.title: useOptimistic
cards.definition: Show an immediate optimistic result while an async action is still running.
points: The optimistic value exists only while the action is in flight; it is discarded when the real result arrives.
React reverts it automatically on failure, so no rollback code is written by hand.
It is a render-time projection, not state — the server's answer remains the source of truth.
useCases: A Like that responds instantly — Waiting 400ms for a round trip makes a button feel broken; showing the new count immediately and correcting on failure is what feels native.

Submitting a form without four state variables — Every mutation needs pending, error, success and optimistic states; Actions supply them so a submit button cannot get stuck spinning after a failed request.

industries.problem: A basket, a price and a stock count have to agree on screen while three people buy the last item; component state keeps one source of truth instead of DOM updates that drift.
Account dashboards mix slow ledger reads with instant balances, and boundaries let the fast half render while the slow half is still loading rather than blanking the page.

cards.title: Amazon S3
cards.definition: Store and retrieve objects such as files, media and datasets.
points: Everything is an API behind an IAM policy. Access is denied by default, and 'AccessDenied' is usually a missing permission on a resource you did not realise was involved.
Regions are separate deployments of the service, and data does not move between them for free. Latency, cost and compliance all follow from the region choice.
Charges come from three places: what you store, what you transfer, and what you run. Egress is the one people forget, and it is often the largest line.
useCases: Static site asset hosting — a React build's hashed JS, CSS and image files are uploaded to a bucket and served through CloudFront with long cache lifetimes.
Data lake landing zone — nightly Parquet exports from an orders database land under date-partitioned prefixes for Athena queries and Glue jobs to read.

industries.problem: Large video masters and transcoded renditions need durable, cheap storage that scales without managing file servers or disk capacity.
Imaging files and trial datasets must be retained durably in an approved region, with encryption and access limited to named roles.

cards.title: Amazon QuickSight
cards.definition: Create and manage business-intelligence datasets, analyses and dashboards.
points: Everything is an API behind an IAM policy. Access is denied by default, and 'AccessDenied' is usually a missing permission on a resource you did not realise was involved.

useCases: Answering questions over collected data — Event and log data become reports and dashboards without loading everything into the production database.
Running a product without owning the hardware — Compute, storage, networking and identity are rented per hour, so a service can start on one instance and grow without a data-centre purchase.

industries.problem: Peak days need ten times the capacity for a few hours, which is a scaling policy rather than a datacentre purchase.
Data residency, encryption and access logging are compliance requirements that arrive as managed service settings instead of a project.

Running a product without owning the hardware — Compute, storage, networking and identity are rented per hour, so a service can start on one instance and grow without a data-centre purchase.

industries.problem: Flash-sale traffic overloads fixed-size ECS services, so task counts must grow with demand and shrink afterward to avoid paying for idle capacity.
Bidding event volume swings by hour, so DynamoDB read and write capacity must follow load to avoid throttled requests without overprovisioning.

cards.title: Amazon Cognito

cards.title: Structured Output Parser
cards.definition: Require an output shape and validate it before handing data to a business system.
points: The model's reply is constrained to a schema.
A schema is what makes the output usable by the next node.
A reply that validates can still be semantically wrong.
useCases: Support ticket triage — an LLM reads an inbound email and must return category, priority enum and summary, so the Switch node can route it to the right Zendesk queue.
Invoice field extraction — a model reads a PDF invoice and returns vendor, invoice_number, total number and ISO date, and a failed parse stops the run before the accounting node.

industries.problem: Claim emails arrive as free text, and a fixed schema turns them into typed fields that the claims system can accept or reject.
Carrier delay notices vary in wording, so schema-validated output yields consistent status codes and dates for shipment tracking updates.

cards.title: Run once versus per item
cards.definition: Choose whether a transformation sees an entire collection or one item at a time.
points: A Code node either runs for all items or once per item.
All-items mode is what allows aggregation across the batch.
Per-item mode silently multiplies any API call inside it.
useCases: Batch total in one pass — a Code node in run-once-for-all-items mode sums line amounts across 500 invoice items and returns one summary item for the finance Slack post.
Per-item geocode call trap — a Code node in per-item mode calls a geocoding API for each of 2,000 contacts, so switching to one batched request cuts the call count.
