industries.problem: Shipment scan events must be grouped by carrier and counted per batch, which only works when the node sees all items together.
Per-item mode would fire one rate-limited FX API call per transaction row, so lookups must be done once for the whole batch.

cards.title: Schedule Trigger
cards.definition: Schedule repeatable jobs with the intended time zone and overlap policy.
points: A workflow runs on an interval or a cron expression.
The trigger only fires while the workflow is active.
A long run overlapping the next tick creates concurrent executions.
useCases: Nightly invoice export — a Schedule Trigger with cron 0 2 * * * and the workflow time zone set to Europe/Berlin pulls yesterday's invoices into a CSV for accounting.
Overlap-safe inventory sync — a 5-minute interval trigger starts a supplier stock sync, with a lock flag checked first so a slow run doesn't overlap the next tick.

industries.problem: Daily price and stock refreshes must fire at local store opening time, so the trigger's time zone must match the stores, not the server.
A reconciliation job that outlasts its interval can run twice at once and double-post ledger entries unless overlap is handled.

cards.title: Item linking
cards.definition: Keep output items connected to their inputs when referencing data from earlier nodes.
points: Output items keep a link back to the input item that produced them.
The link is what lets a later node reach the original data.
Code that rebuilds items without the link breaks that lookup.
useCases: Enriched lead back to its form — after an HTTP Request enriches each lead, a later Slack node uses paired item data to read the original form's message field.
Code node drops the link — a Code node returns fresh objects with only a score field, so $('Webhook').item in the next node throws a paired-item error.

industries.problem: Claim IDs from the intake node must reach the payout step after fraud-check calls, or each result can't be matched to its claim.
After a per-attendee QR code is generated, the email node needs that attendee's name and seat, which needs intact item links.

cards.title: Cloud and self-hosted n8n
cards.definition: Compare managed operation with responsibility for upgrades, backups and security.
points: The hosted service and a self-run instance differ in who operates it.
Self-hosting keeps credentials and data inside your own network.
It also makes upgrades, backups and scaling your responsibility.
useCases: Automating work that spans several systems — A form, a spreadsheet, a CRM and an email tool are connected without a service written, deployed and maintained for the join.
Letting an operations team change the workflow — The steps are visible and editable by the people who own the process, instead of queued behind engineering for every rule change.

industries.problem: Order, payment and shipping events arrive out of order and more than once, so idempotent retried handling is what keeps the order state correct.
Onboarding, trial reminders and dunning are multi-day sequences, which a durable workflow survives and a cron job plus a database flag does not.

cards.title: Webhook authentication
cards.definition: Verify callers and validate payloads before performing downstream actions.
points: Header, basic or signature checks guard the endpoint.
An unauthenticated webhook is an open endpoint anyone may call.
A shared secret in a query string is logged everywhere the URL is.
useCases: Stripe signature check — an n8n Webhook node passes the raw body and signature header through a Code node that verifies the HMAC before an order is marked paid.
Header token gate for form posts — a Webhook node using Header Auth rejects requests missing the secret, so a public site form can't spam the CRM.

industries.problem: Forged payment or shipment webhooks could mark unpaid orders as fulfilled unless each caller's signature is verified first.
An open intake webhook could accept fake patient records, so callers must be authenticated before data reaches scheduling systems.

cards.title: Aggregate and Split Out
cards.definition: Convert between grouped records and individual items with stable identifiers.
points: Many items combine into one, or one item splits into many.
They are the pair that changes the shape between per-item and per-batch work.
Aggregating loses per-item linking to the original input.
useCases: Order lines to Slack digest — a Shopify order's line_items array is split out so each SKU gets a stock check, then aggregated into one summary message.
Batch insert after enrichment — an enrichment API returns a lead list that is aggregated into one array so a single bulk-insert call replaces hundreds of row-by-row writes.

industries.problem: A shipment manifest holds many parcels in one record, and splitting it out lets each parcel get its own tracking lookup and status update.
Invoice line items must be checked one by one against tax codes, then regrouped into a single total per invoice for the ledger entry.

cards.title: Templates and reusable workflows
cards.definition: Adapt a template by checking credentials, field mappings and error behavior.
points: A template is a starting point that is copied rather than referenced.
Copying means later template fixes do not reach the copies.
A sub-workflow is the mechanism when genuine reuse is wanted.
useCases: Template adopted for a new client — a team copies a Typeform-to-HubSpot template, then reselects the HubSpot credential, remaps renamed form fields and adds an error branch before activating.
Fix that never reaches copies — a pagination bug is patched in the original template, but five workflows copied from it still carry the bug until someone updates each one by hand.

industries.problem: Each client needs a near-identical onboarding automation, and copying a template without rechecking credentials risks writing to the wrong client account.
Teams copy a ticket-routing template into several products, and a later fix stays out of the copies unless shared logic sits in a sub-workflow.

cards.title: OAuth2 and credential scopes
cards.definition: Grant only required access and plan credential renewal and revocation.
points: Credentials are stored centrally and scoped to what they need.
Central storage is what keeps a secret out of the workflow JSON.
A token that expires needs refresh configured or the workflow fails later.
useCases: Read-only Google Sheets scope — a weekly report workflow uses an OAuth2 credential limited to spreadsheets.readonly so a leaked token can't edit or delete any sheets.
Refresh token for Gmail triage — an n8n workflow labels incoming support mail, and offline access with refresh is set up so it doesn't fail after the access token expires.

industries.problem: Accounting sync workflows need ledger access, but a broad token could modify records, so scoped credentials plus revocation limit exposure.
Course automations touching Google Classroom and Drive must use minimum scopes so a staff departure can be handled by revoking one credential.

cards.title: Upgrades and rollback
cards.definition: Back up first, test workflow compatibility and retain a recovery plan for upgrades.
points: Versions are upgraded deliberately with a way back.
Node behaviour can change between versions in ways workflows notice.
A database migrated forward may not accept the previous version.
useCases: Staging rehearsal before upgrade — clone the production n8n database and workflows into a staging container, run the new version, and replay key workflows to catch changed node output.
Snapshot-based rollback — take a Postgres dump and pin the previous Docker image tag before upgrading, so a failed migration can be reverted by restoring both together.

industries.problem: A node behavior change after an upgrade could silently alter reconciliation workflows, so versions are tested and reversible before touching ledgers.
Shipment-tracking automations must keep running, so a bad n8n upgrade needs a database backup and tested restore path to avoid prolonged downtime.

cards.title: n8n workflow architecture
cards.definition: Connect trigger and action nodes into an automation with explicit data and error paths.
points: A workflow is nodes connected by the data that flows between them.
Every node receives items and emits items, which is what makes them composable.
A node with no incoming connection never runs, however correct it is.
useCases: Automating work that spans several systems — A form, a spreadsheet, a CRM and an email tool are connected without a service written, deployed and maintained for the join.
Letting an operations team change the workflow — The steps are visible and editable by the people who own the process, instead of queued behind engineering for every rule change.

industries.problem: Order, payment and shipping events arrive out of order and more than once, so idempotent retried handling is what keeps the order state correct.
Onboarding, trial reminders and dunning are multi-day sequences, which a durable workflow survives and a cron job plus a database flag does not.

cards.title: Queue mode and Redis
cards.definition: Separate incoming execution coordination from worker processing using queue infrastructure.
points: The main instance generates an execution and passes its id to Redis rather than running it.
`EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue` is required on the main instance and on every worker.
The docs advise against queue mode on SQLite; a server database is expected.
useCases: Webhook burst absorption — a marketing form webhook receives thousands of submissions at once and the main instance queues execution ids in Redis while workers drain them.
Scaling heavy workflows — a nightly ETL that syncs large CRM exports runs on added worker containers so the editor and webhook intake on the main instance stay responsive.

industries.problem: Flash-sale order webhooks arrive in spikes, and queued executions in Redis keep orders from being dropped while workers catch up.
Appointment and lab-result sync jobs vary in length, so separate workers stop long runs from blocking time-sensitive intake workflows.

cards.title: Docker deployment
cards.definition: Run n8n with persistent storage and deployment-specific environment configuration.
points: Redis runs on localhost port 6379 with no password by default.
It can run on a separate machine so long as the n8n instances can reach it.
Persistent state must be mounted, or it is lost when the container is replaced.
useCases: Volume-mounted data directory — a compose file maps /home/node/.n8n to a named volume so credentials and the encryption key survive an image upgrade.
Per-environment compose config — staging and production containers get different WEBHOOK_URL, timezone and database env vars from separate .env files.

industries.problem: Each client needs an isolated n8n container whose credentials and workflows persist across upgrades and host reboots.
Internal automations must run on a self-hosted container with pinned config and persisted state, so data stays in-house and redeploys lose nothing.

cards.title: Manual and production executions
cards.definition: Distinguish test runs from active production triggers and their side effects.
points: A manual run is triggered from the editor; a production run by its trigger.
Manual runs let you inspect data before the workflow is active.
Only an active workflow responds to its production trigger.
useCases: Automating work that spans several systems — A form, a spreadsheet, a CRM and an email tool are connected without a service written, deployed and maintained for the join.
Letting an operations team change the workflow — The steps are visible and editable by the people who own the process, instead of queued behind engineering for every rule change.

industries.problem: Order, payment and shipping events arrive out of order and more than once, so idempotent retried handling is what keeps the order state correct.
Onboarding, trial reminders and dunning are multi-day sequences, which a durable workflow survives and a cron job plus a database flag does not.

cards.title: while loops
cards.definition: Repeats while a condition holds.
points: The body repeats while a condition stays true.
It is the right loop when the number of iterations is not known in advance.
A condition that never changes inside the body never terminates.
useCases: Retry until ready — a deploy script polls a service health endpoint in a while loop, sleeping 2 seconds between checks until it returns 200 or a deadline passes.
Queue drain worker — a consumer runs while the task queue is not empty, popping one job at a time, since new jobs may arrive while it processes.

industries.problem: A game loop must keep updating and rendering frames until the player quits, and the number of frames is unknown beforehand.
Reconnect logic must keep retrying a dropped device link with backoff until it succeeds, and the number of attempts cannot be predicted.

cards.title: Booleans & truthiness
cards.definition: Empty collections, 0 and None are falsy; almost everything else is truthy.
points: Empty containers, zero and None are falsy without being False.
Testing a container directly is idiomatic; comparing its length is not.
An identity check against True is stricter than truthiness and usually wrong.
useCases: Empty search guard — a handler runs 'if not results:' to show a 'no matches' message when the query returns an empty list, with no len() comparison.
Flag check pitfall — a webhook payload field 'active' arrives as 1 from one sender, so 'if flag is True' wrongly rejects it while 'if flag' accepts it.

industries.problem: Checkout code must tell an empty cart from a populated one, and testing the list directly avoids clumsy length checks on every branch.
Patient records often have blank or zero lab fields, so truthiness checks must be deliberate to avoid treating a valid 0 result as missing data.

cards.title: Lists
cards.definition: Ordered, mutable sequences.
points: A list is an ordered, mutable sequence that can hold mixed types.
Appending is cheap; inserting at the front shifts every element.
Copying is shallow, so nested objects are still shared.
useCases: Undo history stack — a text editor appends each edit to a list and pops the last one on Ctrl+Z, using the cheap end of the list.
Shallow-copy gotcha — copying a list of cart-line dicts with list(cart) still shares each dict, so a price edit in the copy changes the original.

industries.problem: A till builds a basket as items are scanned in order, and needs to void or add lines before the receipt prints.
Turn-based games keep a player's ordered hand or action queue that grows and shrinks, so it needs a mutable, indexable sequence.

cards.title: Generators
cards.definition: yield produces values lazily, one at a time, so a pipeline can process more data than fits in memory.
points: yield produces values lazily, one at a time, keeping state between them.
Nothing runs until the generator is iterated.
Memory stays constant regardless of how many values are produced.
useCases: Streaming log parser — a generator reads a multi-gigabyte access log line by line and yields only parsed 5xx entries to a counter.
Chunked CSV import — yield batches of 1,000 rows from a huge file so each batch is validated and inserted without loading the whole file.

industries.problem: Exporting millions of order records for reporting would exhaust memory, so rows are yielded and written to the file incrementally.
Sequencing files are too large to load whole, so generators yield one read at a time for filtering and quality checks.

cards.title: Slicing
cards.definition: seq[start:stop:step] on any sequence, with stop exclusive.
points: A slice takes a start, a stop and a step, and the stop is excluded.
Out-of-range bounds clamp rather than raise, unlike indexing.
Slicing a list copies it; slicing a string makes a new string.
useCases: Choosing the structure for the lookup — A list scan where a dict lookup belongs is the difference between a report that runs in a second and one that runs in a minute.
Scripting, data work and backend services — The language reached for when the job is automation, analysis or an API, and readability matters more than raw speed.

industries.problem: A notebook that runs today must run on a colleague's machine tomorrow, which locked and resolved dependencies give and a list of installs does not.
Numerical work depends on exact library versions, so an unpinned upgrade that silently changes a result is a retracted paper rather than a bug.

cards.title: Comprehensions
cards.definition: List, dict, set and generator comprehensions build a collection from an iterable in one expression.
points: A new list, set or dictionary is built from an expression over an iterable.
It reads as a single expression, which is why it beats an append loop.
Nesting more than two levels is usually less readable than the loop.
useCases: Index by ID — a dict comprehension turns a list of user records from an API into {user['id']: user} for constant-time lookups during enrichment.
Unique domains — a set comprehension over a list of signup emails extracts lowercased domains, removing duplicates in a single expression.

industries.problem: Raw event lists need filtering and reshaping into per-page dicts, and a comprehension replaces several lines of append-loop boilerplate.
Gradebook exports need passing scores picked out and renamed per student, and a comprehension does that in one readable line.

cards.title: NumPy
cards.definition: N-dimensional arrays with vectorised operations that run in C.
points: Arrays hold uniform types and operate element-wise without loops.
Vectorised operations run in compiled code, which is the speed.
A slice is a view, so writing through it changes the original.
useCases: Image brightness adjustment — scale a 1080p photo's pixel array by a gain factor and clip to 0-255 in one expression, with no per-pixel Python loop.
Sensor data normalisation — subtract each column's mean and divide by its standard deviation across a 2D array of temperature readings via broadcasting.

industries.problem: Computing daily returns and rolling covariance across thousands of tickers in pure Python loops is too slow for overnight risk runs.
Applying windowing and thresholds to large 3D CT volumes needs fast array math that loops over voxels cannot deliver.

cards.title: Dictionaries
cards.definition: Hash maps from keys to values, insertion-ordered since 3.7.
points: Keys map to values with average constant-time lookup.
Insertion order is preserved, which is guaranteed and not incidental.
Keys must be hashable, which rules out lists and dictionaries.
useCases: Word frequency counter — loop over log lines and use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1 to tally each distinct error code in one pass.
JSON config lookup — json.loads returns nested dicts, and a service reads settings['db']['host'] by key, with .get() supplying a default for missing options.

industries.problem: Counting millions of events per user or error code needs fast keyed lookups instead of rescanning a list for each event.
Incoming JSON payloads have named fields in varying shapes, and dict keys let code read, default, and reorder them without positional assumptions.

cards.title: for loops
cards.definition: Iterates over any iterable rather than counting indices.
points: A for loop iterates over an iterable rather than over an index.
Iterating directly avoids the off-by-one that index arithmetic invites.
Mutating the sequence while looping over it skips elements.
useCases: Parallel list walk — zip a list of invoice IDs with a list of payment amounts in one for loop, so no index arithmetic can misalign the pairs.
Safe pruning of a cart — loop over a copy of a shopping cart's items with list(cart) to remove out-of-stock entries without skipping the item after each removal.

industries.problem: Triage scripts walk every ticket in an exported queue, and looping directly over tickets avoids the off-by-one errors that index loops invite.
Stock reconciliation must check each bin in a location list, and mutating that list mid-loop would silently skip bins and leave counts wrong.

cards.title: if / elif / else
cards.definition: Branching on truthiness, with no switch needed.
points: Branches are tested in order and the first match wins.
Indentation is the block structure, so it is syntax rather than style.
A conditional expression is the one-line form for choosing a value.
useCases: Shipping fee tiers — an order function checks if total >= 100, elif total >= 50, else, so each cart gets exactly one shipping rate from the first matching band.
HTTP status handler — a response checker uses if code == 200, elif code == 404, else to return data, raise NotFound, or log an unexpected failure.

industries.problem: Triage code must map a patient's vitals to one priority level, and ordered elif checks stop at the first severe reading matched.
Usage bills apply different per-unit rates by consumption band, and an if/elif/else ladder picks exactly one rate for each meter reading.

cards.title: Functions
cards.definition: def creates a function object you can pass around.
points: A function groups behaviour behind a name and returns a value.
A function without an explicit return returns None.
Defining one binds a name like any other assignment.
useCases: Reusable validator — define a function that checks an incoming order dict and returns True or False, so every endpoint applies the same rule.
Callback table — store function objects in a dict keyed by event name, then look up and call the right handler for each message.

industries.problem: Pricing rules for discounts and tax are copied across checkout code, so a named function keeps one tested calculation.
Cleaning steps for messy CSV columns get repeated per file, so small functions can be named, reused and passed into pipelines.

cards.title: itertools
cards.definition: Lazy building blocks for iteration — chain, groupby, product, islice — that compose pipelines without materialising the intermediate lists.
points: Iterator building blocks compose lazily over any iterable.
Nothing is materialised, so infinite sequences are usable.
chain, groupby and islice replace a lot of manual loop bookkeeping.
useCases: Merge rotated logs — chain.from_iterable streams several multi-gigabyte log files as one sequence without concatenating them in memory.
Group sorted events — groupby on a pre-sorted CSV of transactions yields per-customer batches for summaries without building a dict of lists.

industries.problem: Chains rotated log files into one lazy stream so huge archives can be scanned without loading them into memory.
Product generates hyperparameter combinations lazily, so large search grids can be run without storing every configuration.

cards.title: Variables & assignment
cards.definition: Names bound to objects.
points: A name is bound to an object; it is not a box holding a value.
Two names can bind the same object, so mutating through one is visible through the other.
Rebinding a name never affects the object it used to point at.
useCases: Writing a script someone else can read — Names, values and formatting decide whether a one-off script survives being handed to a colleague.
Scripting, data work and backend services — The language reached for when the job is automation, analysis or an API, and readability matters more than raw speed.

industries.problem: A notebook that runs today must run on a colleague's machine tomorrow, which locked and resolved dependencies give and a list of installs does not.
Numerical work depends on exact library versions, so an unpinned upgrade that silently changes a result is a retracted paper rather than a bug.

cards.title: Recursion
cards.definition: A function calling itself, bounded by a base case.
points: A function calls itself on a smaller version of the problem.
A base case is what stops it, and its absence is a recursion error.
Python has a recursion limit and does not optimise tail calls.
useCases: Nested category tree — a function walks a product category dict whose children may have their own children, summing item counts at every depth.
Config file merging — a function merges nested override dicts into defaults by calling itself whenever both values are dicts, stopping at plain values.

industries.problem: Backup and cleanup tools must visit folders of unknown depth, and recursion handles each subfolder the same way as its parent.
Arithmetic and code expressions nest inside each other, so a recursive evaluator on the syntax tree handles any depth with one rule.

cards.title: Sets
cards.definition: Unordered collections of unique hashable values, with union, intersection and difference as operators.
points: A set holds unique, unordered, hashable members.
Membership is constant time, which is why it beats a list for lookups.
Union, intersection and difference express set logic directly.
useCases: Deduplicating event IDs — a webhook consumer keeps a set of processed event IDs so retried deliveries are skipped in constant time.
Permission diffing — compare a user's current role permissions with the required set using difference to list exactly what is missing.

industries.problem: Finding customers who viewed a product but never bought it by taking the difference of two sets of user IDs.
Matching millions of log entries against known malicious IP addresses quickly using constant-time set membership.

cards.title: globalSetup and globalTeardown
cards.definition: Run Playwright setup once before all tests and cleanup once afterward.
points: Configure `globalSetup` when a resource or service must be prepared once before the complete test run.
Configure `globalTeardown` for one-time cleanup after every test has finished.
The setup module contract is one exported function receiving the configuration object.
useCases: Database preparation — Create or seed shared test data before browser tests begin.
Shared service startup — Launch a service or reserve a port needed by the entire run.

industries.problem: Checkout suites need a seeded product catalog and test payment sandbox ready once, not rebuilt before each spec.
Browser tests of patient portals need synthetic records created once and purged afterward so no test data lingers.

cards.title: Pages and popups
cards.definition: Playwright models each tab or popup as a Page inside a BrowserContext.
points: Treat a browser context as a container for several tabs or popup windows, each represented by its own Page object.
Use the Page API for navigation and content interaction regardless of whether the underlying browser surface is a tab or popup.
Subscribe at BrowserContext scope when the test must discover pages created anywhere in that context.
useCases: Handle target=_blank navigation — A test clicks a link that opens a new tab and must verify the destination.
Interact with an opener-specific popup — A workflow opens a child window whose controls must be exercised after creation.

industries.problem: Payment approval opens a bank-hosted 3-D Secure window, and tests need to drive that window then confirm the original checkout page updates.
Opening a contract preview launches a separate viewer tab, and tests must check its content without losing the original file list page.

cards.title: Network interception
cards.definition: Playwright network routing lets tests observe, forward, mock, modify, or fail matching HTTP and HTTPS requests.
points: Network interception supports observing and changing both HTTP and HTTPS traffic.
Page-generated XHR and fetch traffic can be monitored, modified, or handled by routes.
Choose page routing for local scope or context routing for all pages in the context.
useCases: Mock successful responses — Return stable API data without contacting a backend.
Test failure handling — Return an error or terminate a request deliberately.

industries.problem: Checkout tests need payment gateway declines and slow shipping-rate responses that the real sandbox cannot reproduce on demand.
Patient portal tests must run without real records, so API responses are replaced with synthetic data to avoid exposing PHI.

cards.title: Playwright Test configuration
cards.definition: Playwright Test configuration centralizes run-wide defaults and project-specific variants.
points: Export the Playwright Test configuration from the project config file to centralize test-run settings.
Use projects to execute the same suite against separate browser or device profiles.
Set reporter to choose how test execution results are presented, including built-in or custom reporters.
useCases: Run the same tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit projects. — Cross-browser coverage
Apply device profiles to emulate desktop, tablet, or mobile environments. — Responsive UI testing

industries.problem: Checkout regressions must be caught per browser, and one config lets CI publish per-project results to release gates.
Patient portal teams need one suite aimed at staging or a local build with consistent timeouts and retries.

cards.title: Authentication state
cards.definition: Reuse a prepared authenticated browser state so tests skip repeated login while retaining Playwright’s isolated browser contexts.
points: Tests can start with a previously captured authenticated session instead of performing login each time.
The login routine creates a reusable state artifact on disk.
Applying the artifact makes tests begin in a signed-in condition.
useCases: Shared authenticated account — A suite has many tests that require the same signed-in user.
Per-worker authentication — Parallel execution needs independent users rather than one account shared by workers.

industries.problem: Login requires one-time codes and is rate-limited, so reusing a saved signed-in session avoids lockouts across many account-page tests.
Single sign-on redirects slow every test, so a saved session lets hundreds of dashboard checks start already signed in.

cards.title: Parallel workers
cards.definition: Playwright Test uses independent worker processes to run tests concurrently.
points: Parallel execution is built into Playwright Test.
The runner scales execution by starting multiple workers concurrently.
Every worker receives the same environment but owns a separate browser instance.
useCases: Speed up independent test suites — A suite contains many independent tests spread across files.
Serialize access with named locks — Several tests need the same external service or account that rejects concurrent access.

industries.problem: Checkout, search and cart regression suites grow large, and parallel workers keep them fast enough to run on every pull request.
Hundreds of independent portal tests must finish quickly, so workers run files concurrently without delaying release approvals.

cards.title: Projects and browsers
cards.definition: Playwright projects let one test suite run under multiple browser, device, environment, or authentication configurations.
points: Each project names a group of tests that shares one configuration.
Projects let one suite cover different browser engines and device profiles.
Declare the project matrix in the Playwright configuration file.
useCases: Run the suite on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. — Browser compatibility
Reuse tests with emulated desktop, tablet, and mobile devices. — Responsive behavior

industries.problem: Customer and back-office portals share flows but need different logins and base URLs, which projects keep separate in one run.
A player site must work in Safari-based browsers and on TV-sized viewports, so projects pair engines with screen profiles.

cards.title: Locator filtering
cards.definition: Use locator.filter() to narrow repeated components by descendant text or a related locator.
points: filter() refines an existing locator rather than starting a new page-wide search.
Multiple filters can be chained to express several conditions on the same repeated component.
hasText checks text in the component’s own content and descendants.
useCases: Select one repeated component by its text — A page renders many cards, rows, or list items with the same structure.
Select by a descendant locator — The identifying property is a child control such as a button or checkbox.

industries.problem: Ticket queues show many identical rows, so tests need to act on the one matching a ticket subject and status.
Shipment tables repeat the same row layout, and tests must act on the row with a specific tracking number and button.

cards.title: Visual comparisons
cards.definition: Playwright visual comparisons capture a page or element screenshot and compare it with a stored reference.
points: The feature is built into the Playwright Test runner and is intended for screenshot-based visual regression checks.
Pass a stable name to the assertion when the default snapshot naming does not express the scenario clearly.
Unspecified snapshot output uses PNG, giving baselines a predictable default format.
useCases: Full-page visual regression — Detect unintended CSS, layout, or rendering changes on a full page during regression tests.
Focused region checks — Lock a critical component or region without making unrelated page changes part of the baseline.

industries.problem: Theme or CSS updates can silently shift balance tables and disclaimer text on account pages, which screenshot baselines catch before release.
Template and font changes can break article layouts, ad slots, or image cropping across many pages that functional assertions would never flag.

cards.title: Tracing and debugging
cards.definition: Playwright tracing records browser actions and network activity into an archive for Trace Viewer.
points: Begin recording before the interactions you need to diagnose; actions performed earlier will not appear in that trace.
Finish the capture explicitly and write the trace archive so Trace Viewer can open it.
Enable screenshots to create visual timeline evidence that shows how the page appeared during actions.
useCases: Diagnose CI-only failures — A test fails intermittently in CI and needs evidence from the failing retry.
Inspect action timing and page state — A click or navigation behaves differently from expected and the failure location is unclear.

industries.problem: Seat selection fails only after a slow fare-check call; trace screenshots show the stale page when the click fired.
Multi-step quote forms fail late in the flow; a trace shows which earlier step left the page in a broken state.

cards.title: Authentication in a setup project
cards.definition: Authenticate once in a Playwright setup project, save the browser state, and configure dependent projects to use it through storageState.
points: Put the sign-in flow in a setup project so the authenticated context can be reused by later tests.
Declare the setup project as a dependency of each project that needs authenticated browser contexts.
Project dependencies establish ordering: setup executes before the dependent test projects.
useCases: Share one account state across tests — A suite has many tests that all require the same signed-in user.
Avoid repeated login work — Authentication is expensive or rate-limited.

industries.problem: Reservation tests need a logged-in loyalty member, and one saved session avoids repeating the multi-step login before every itinerary check.
Course pages sit behind an identity provider, so a setup project signs in a student once and lets lesson and grading tests start authenticated.

cards.title: Downloads and uploads
cards.definition: Capture browser downloads by waiting for the download event before triggering the action, then inspect the Download object or save the file to a chosen path.
points: Listen for the download event to observe every attachment initiated by the page.
The Download object provides the URL, suggested filename, and access to the downloaded payload.
Set downloadsPath at browser launch when a configured persistence location is preferable.
useCases: Validate generated downloads — A test must verify that clicking an export control produces the expected artifact.
Persist files for later assertions — A test suite needs downloadable artifacts retained after a browser context closes.

industries.problem: Monthly ledger exports must contain correct columns and totals, and tests need to open the downloaded file to confirm it.
Payroll portals let staff download payslip PDFs, and tests must confirm each file name and payload belong to the right employee.

cards.title: Trace viewer
cards.definition: Trace Viewer is Playwright’s GUI for replaying a recorded test trace.
points: It is a graphical interface for investigating a completed test run rather than a live browser-control API.
The timeline supports time-based navigation across individual test actions.
Per-step diagnostics include logs, source, network requests, errors, and console output.
useCases: Diagnose CI failures — A test fails in CI and an artifact contains its trace ZIP.
Inspect action timing and DOM state — An action behaves unexpectedly and its page state must be reconstructed.

industries.problem: Flight search tests fail only in CI when fare requests return late, and traces show which call lagged behind the UI.
Multi-step claim forms break on one step, and traces show the console error and request that preceded the failed click.

cards.title: Test hooks
cards.definition: Use beforeEach and afterEach for scoped per-test setup and cleanup.
points: Fixtures establish the environment required by each test and keep that setup isolated.
A hook can request fixtures through its argument object, just like a test function.
A fixture owns both lifecycle phases, making resource cleanup adjacent to resource creation.
useCases: Scoped per-test preparation — A group of tests needs the same navigation, authentication, or test data preparation before every case.
Per-test cleanup — Each test creates browser state or another resource that must be removed regardless of the test outcome.

industries.problem: Board tests create tasks and comments, and afterEach cleanup stops leftovers from changing counts in later tests.
Each search test needs a fresh itinerary form and cleared saved trips, which beforeEach restores before every case.

cards.title: Browser contexts
cards.definition: Browser contexts are isolated, incognito-like sessions for Playwright tests and scenarios.
points: Each test can begin in a clean context, making its browser state independent from other tests.
Context isolation includes local storage, session storage, and cookies, not only the visible page.
Multiple isolated scenarios can share one browser process without sharing context state.
useCases: Test isolation — Run each test with independent browser state so cookies or storage from one test cannot affect another.
Multi-user workflows — Open separate contexts for two users and exercise their interaction in one scenario.

industries.problem: Buyer and seller chat flows need two separate sessions at once, so messages can be sent and seen without logins colliding.
Concurrent seat-hold tests need several isolated visitors competing for one seat, without shared carts or cookies leaking between them.

cards.title: BrowserContext
cards.definition: Where isolation lives: `storageState`, geolocation, permissions, viewport and offline mode.
points: Cookies, storage, permissions and geolocation are scoped here.
Storage state is loaded and saved at this level, not per page.
Closing it closes every page it owns.
useCases: Geolocation-based store locator — A test grants geolocation to one context at a fixed coordinate and checks that the nearest-branch list appears for that location.
Offline mode behavior — A test sets one context offline mid-session and asserts that a note-taking app queues edits and shows a sync-pending banner.

industries.problem: Courier-tracking maps and delivery-zone checks depend on location, so tests need a fixed geolocation and permission per context.
Technician apps must keep working in dead zones, so tests switch a context offline to confirm job updates are queued and later synced.

cards.title: --repeat-each
cards.definition: Runs a test many times to prove whether it is genuinely flaky.
points: Each test runs several times in one invocation.
Repetition is how a suspected flake is confirmed.
A test passing ten times is not proof it cannot fail.
useCases: Confirm a suspected flake — Run one intermittently failing checkout test 50 times in a single command to see whether and how often it fails.
Verify a flake fix — After adding a proper wait for a lazy-loaded table, repeat the edited spec many times to check the intermittent failure is gone.

industries.problem: A live driver-map test fails once in a while, and repeated runs show whether it is real flakiness or a one-off CI glitch.
A transfer confirmation test sometimes fails after a race with a balance refresh, so repeated runs prove the fix before merging.

cards.title: Trace Viewer
cards.definition: Replays a run with DOM snapshots, network, console and a timeline per action.
points: Actions, snapshots, network and console are replayed from a trace.
The DOM snapshot per step shows the page as the test saw it.
It only exists if tracing was enabled for that run.
useCases: Step through a failed retry offline — Open the trace ZIP from a nightly run and click through each action to see which locator resolved to the wrong element.
Compare before and after DOM snapshots — Hover an action in the timeline to see the page before and after a form submit, revealing a validation message that never rendered.

industries.problem: Order tracking tests fail when a map widget loads late, and the trace shows the pending request and half-rendered page at the failed click.
Property search filters misbehave only on some runs, and per-step snapshots reveal which listing state the test saw when its assertion failed.

cards.title: page.exposeFunction
cards.definition: Installs a Node callback the page can call, for bridging back out.
points: A Node function is callable from inside the page.
It is how page code reports back into the test process.
It stays bound for the page's lifetime, including after navigation.
useCases: Capture analytics beacons — expose a Node function so page code forwards each tracking event to the test, which asserts the event payload and order.
Bridge a canvas editor callback — a drawing app calls the exposed function on every save, letting the test read serialized document state from Node.

industries.problem: Tag scripts fire impression callbacks inside the page, and tests need those payloads delivered to Node to verify targeting values.
A browser game engine emits score and match-end events internally, and tests need them sent to Node to assert outcomes without scraping the UI.

cards.title: Authentication reuse
cards.definition: Signing in once in a setup project and reusing the state is the single biggest speed win.
points: Signing in once and reusing the saved state removes the slowest step from every test.
The docs authenticate in a clean context by passing `storageState: undefined`.
Waiting for the final URL matters, because a login can set cookies across redirects.
useCases: Clean-context login test — A spec for the sign-in form sets storageState to undefined so saved cookies do not bypass it.
Wait for final URL — Setup awaits the dashboard URL after login redirects so every cookie exists before state is saved.

industries.problem: Tax portal sign-in bounces through an ID service; saving state before the last redirect leaves tests signed out.
Self-service tests start signed in, but login-error checks need a clean context so the form actually appears.

cards.title: expect.soft
cards.definition: Records a failure and carries on, so one run reports every problem.
points: A failed assertion records but does not stop the test.
Several failures can be reported from one run.
The test still fails, so a soft assertion is not an ignored one.
useCases: Audit a settings page in one pass — a test checks the heading, each toggle's default state and the footer links with expect.soft, so one run lists every wrong default.
Validate a confirmation summary — after an order form submits, soft assertions check name, address, total and delivery date so every wrong field appears in a single report.

industries.problem: A policy quote summary shows many computed fields, and soft assertions list every wrong premium line in one run instead of the first.
Property listing pages need price, address, photo count and agent details verified together, so one run exposes every broken field.

cards.title: Accessibility scanning
cards.definition: `@axe-core/playwright` runs an audit inside an existing test.
points: Automated accessibility checks run against a page.
It catches a real subset of issues very cheaply.
Most accessibility problems are not machine-detectable.
useCases: Scan key pages on every pull request — After the login and checkout tests load each page, an axe audit fails the build when a new image lacks alt text or a form input lacks a label.
Scan a modal in its open state — A test opens a cookie preferences dialog, then audits only that element to catch low color contrast and missing ARIA names.

industries.problem: Public forms must meet accessibility rules, and automated scans catch missing labels and contrast failures before each release.
Course registration pages change often, and a cheap per-build audit flags new ARIA and heading errors that would block students using screen readers.

cards.title: Auto-waiting
cards.definition: Let Playwright wait for actionable, stable elements instead of adding arbitrary sleeps.
points: Playwright waits for an element to be actionable before acting on it.
Actionable means attached, visible, stable and able to receive the event.
An arbitrary sleep is both slower than needed and still sometimes too short.
useCases: Proving a real user journey still works — Sign in, search, add to basket, pay: the flows that matter cross pages and services, and only a browser can check them end to end.
Finding out why a test failed — Traces, videos and the inspector show the run rather than a stack trace, which is what makes a flaky failure diagnosable.

industries.problem: Seat maps and fare panels redraw after each selection, so fixed sleeps either slow tests or click while the page is mid-update.
Appointment slots load asynchronously and animate in, and auto-waiting prevents clicks on slots that are not yet visible or stable.

cards.title: toBeChecked
cards.definition: Asserts checkbox and radio state, including indeterminate.
points: A checkbox or radio state is asserted.
It reads the control's real state rather than a class.
Indeterminate is a third state neither checked nor unchecked.
useCases: Terms consent gate — After a signup form is submitted with the consent box ticked, assert the checkbox reads checked and the submit button is enabled.
Select-all indeterminate state — Tick two of five rows in a table and assert the header checkbox is indeterminate, not checked or unchecked.

industries.problem: Subscription preference centers must keep opt-in boxes accurate, or users get mail they declined or miss mail they wanted.
Intake forms with allergy and consent checkboxes need verified saved selections so a wrongly cleared box does not hide patient information.

cards.title: Docker image
cards.definition: The official image ships the browsers and system dependencies, so CI matches local runs.
points: An official image carries the browsers and their dependencies.
It is what makes local and CI runs match.
The image version must track the library version.
useCases: Pin image to library version — A team upgrades @playwright/test in package.json and bumps the mcr.microsoft.com/playwright tag to the same version so browser builds still match.
Run the suite in a CI container — A pipeline job starts from the official Playwright image so Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and system fonts are present without any install step.

industries.problem: Contributors on macOS, Windows and Linux see different rendering, and one shared image gives CI a single browser environment.
Locked-down build servers cannot download browsers at run time, so a prebuilt image supplies them and keeps accessibility tests reproducible.

cards.title: test.beforeEach / afterEach
cards.definition: Per-test setup and teardown, with fixtures available in both.
points: Setup and teardown run around each test.
They run inside the test's own context, so nothing leaks onward.
Work here is paid once per test, not once per file.
useCases: Reset a wizard form before each test — beforeEach opens the signup wizard at step one so every case starts from the same empty form and step counter.
Log and clear a test-created session — afterEach reads the test's fixture page state, attaches the console log on failure, then closes the context cleanly.

industries.problem: Applicant tracker tests each add candidates to a pipeline, and per-test setup and teardown keep stage counts from drifting between cases.
Each booking test needs an empty cart and a fresh promo-code state, which per-test hooks provide without one test inheriting another's holds.

cards.title: fill
cards.definition: Sets an input's value in one step.
points: An input's value is set and the input event dispatched.
It clears first, so it replaces rather than appends.
It does not produce per-key events, which some inputs rely on.
useCases: Replace a prefilled field — a profile test calls fill on an email input holding an old address and asserts only the new address remains, with no leftover text.
Bulk-enter a long form — a signup test fills name, address and a 500-character bio quickly, then asserts the input-driven live validation messages disappear.

industries.problem: Loan application forms have many prefilled numeric fields, and tests must overwrite amounts cleanly rather than append digits to stale values.
Candidate profile forms hold long free-text fields, and tests need fast entry that still triggers the input event driving character counters.

cards.title: browser.newContext
cards.definition: An isolated profile — its own cookies, storage and permissions.
points: An isolated profile is created with its own cookies and storage.
Isolation per context is what makes parallel tests independent.
A context is cheap; a browser launch is not.
useCases: Per-test fresh context — each spec calls browser.newContext() on one shared browser so a cart or login from one test never appears in the next.
Locale and timezone variants — create a context with a German locale and Berlin timezone to check that a booking page formats dates and currency correctly.

industries.problem: Teacher and student dashboards must be tested at once, and separate contexts keep their sessions from overwriting each other.
Account portal tests across many plans need clean sessions fast, so each test gets a new context instead of a slow browser relaunch.

cards.title: toHaveCount
cards.definition: Asserts how many elements a locator matches — the assertion for list rendering.
points: The exact number of matching elements is asserted, with retries.
Retrying is what lets it wait for a list to finish rendering.
Zero is a valid count, which is how absence of a list is asserted.
useCases: Wait for search results to finish — after submitting a query, a test asserts the results list holds exactly 10 items, retrying until pagination rendering settles.
Assert an empty cart list — after removing the last item, a test expects the cart row locator to have count 0, proving the line items are gone.

industries.problem: Filtering listings re-renders the results list asynchronously, so tests need to wait for the exact number of postings before checking them.
After deleting or archiving messages, tests must confirm the inbox rows shrink to the right count, including zero when the folder is emptied.

cards.title: Blob reports
cards.definition: Sharded runs emit blobs that `merge-reports` combines into one HTML report.
points: Shard results are emitted for later merging.
Merging is what produces one report from a sharded run.
Without merging, each shard reports only its own slice.
useCases: Merge shard output in CI — A pipeline fans out four sharded jobs that upload blob folders, and a final job downloads them and runs merge-reports to build one HTML report.
Combine nightly regression shards — Ten parallel machines each run a slice of a 3,000-test nightly suite, and their blobs merge into a single report reviewers open the next morning.

industries.problem: A huge cross-device UI suite is split across many CI machines, and blob merging gives QA one report instead of many partial ones.
Long regression runs for invoice and plan-change screens are sharded for speed, and merged blobs give auditors one complete result set per release.

cards.title: getByTestId
cards.definition: Matches an explicit test id.
points: An element is found by a dedicated test attribute.
A test id is the most stable anchor because nothing else uses it.
It says nothing about whether the element is usable or accessible.
useCases: Target a icon-only toolbar button — a rich-text editor's bold and undo buttons have no visible text, so the test clicks them through data-testid values like toolbar-bold.
Pick a chart widget on a dashboard — a analytics page has several identical canvas tiles, and the test reads the one tagged data-testid="revenue-chart" to verify its legend.

industries.problem: Localized labels and redesigned copy keep changing on balance cards, so tests anchor to fixed ids instead of text that translators edit.
Invoice pages render repeated widgets with generated class names, so a dedicated test attribute gives tests one stable handle across releases.

cards.title: projects
cards.definition: Named configurations — one per browser, viewport or setup dependency — run in one command.
points: Named configurations run the same tests differently.
Projects are what make browsers, devices and setup declarative.
Dependencies between projects control ordering.
useCases: Cross-browser matrix — a playwright.config lists chromium, firefox and webkit projects so one npx playwright test run executes the same specs in all three engines.
Mobile versus desktop layouts — a device-emulated project with a phone viewport runs beside a desktop project to check that a navigation menu collapses into a hamburger only on small screens.

industries.problem: Web player controls and layouts differ across desktop and tablet viewports, and named projects run each variant without duplicating specs.
Dashboards need admin and read-only role checks, and a project per role with a setup dependency runs both in order from one command.

cards.title: focus / blur
cards.definition: Moves focus explicitly, for testing keyboard and validation behaviour.
points: Focus is moved to or away from an element.
Blur is what triggers validation that runs on leaving a field.
Focusing directly skips the tab order a keyboard user would follow.
useCases: Trigger on-blur email validation — a signup test focuses the email input, types a malformed address, then blurs it to assert the inline error appears before submit.
Verify a keyboard focus ring — a test focuses a search button directly and asserts the visible focus outline style, without walking the full tab sequence to reach it.

industries.problem: IBAN and card number fields validate when the user leaves them, so tests must blur each field to confirm errors show before a transfer is submitted.
Application forms must work for keyboard-only users, so tests move focus to fields and away to check that error messages and focus indicators appear.

cards.title: browserType.connect
cards.definition: Attaches to a remote browser server, for a grid or a container.
points: A remote browser is driven over a websocket.
Connecting is how a browser grid or container is shared.
Latency per action rises, which changes how a suite feels.
useCases: Shared Selenium-style grid run — a CI job calls browserType.connect with a grid's websocket endpoint so 20 parallel workers use pooled browsers instead of installing them.
Containerized browser sidecar — tests on a lean Node runner connect to a Playwright server in a separate container, keeping browser dependencies out of the test image.

industries.problem: Security rules block browser installs on build agents, so tests connect to a centrally managed browser pool.
Heavy player tests need strong machines, so lightweight CI runners connect to remote browser hosts and tolerate added per-action latency.

cards.title: Clock API
cards.definition: Controls the page's clock so timers, polling and expiry can be tested deterministically.
points: Time is controlled so timers and dates are deterministic.
Controlling time is what makes a timeout testable in milliseconds.
Installing it affects every timer, including the framework's own.
useCases: Expire a session warning — a test installs the clock, logs in, fast-forwards 14 minutes and asserts the idle-timeout dialog appears without waiting in real time.
Drive a polling status badge — a test advances the fake clock by 5-second steps and asserts a report-generation badge refreshes and flips to Ready once the mocked endpoint changes.

industries.problem: Auto-logout after inactivity must be verified, but real 15-minute waits make the check too slow to run on every build.
Seat holds expire on a countdown, and tests need to jump to zero to confirm released seats without waiting out the timer.

cards.title: page.routeFromHAR
cards.definition: Replays a recorded HAR file, so a whole session can be served offline.
points: Recorded traffic replays as the network layer.
A HAR is a realistic fixture captured from a real session.
It goes stale as the API changes, silently testing an old contract.
useCases: Replay a recorded dashboard session — a test calls routeFromHAR with a HAR captured from a real login and data load, so the analytics page renders offline with realistic responses.
Detect a drifted API contract — a team re-records the HAR after a backend release and diffs it, revealing renamed fields the stale replay had been hiding.

industries.problem: Account pages call many slow, rate-limited APIs, so replaying a recorded session gives stable realistic data without hitting a sandbox.
Shipment tracking screens need large real-world responses, and a HAR replay serves them offline without depending on carrier APIs.

cards.title: Permissions
cards.definition: Grants or denies camera, clipboard, notifications and geolocation per context.
points: Browser permissions are granted or denied for a context.
Granting up front avoids a dialog the test cannot click.
Permissions are per context, so a new context resets them.
useCases: Store locator geolocation — a context grants geolocation with fixed coordinates so a "find stores near me" test lists the nearest branches with no permission prompt.
Clipboard copy button — a test grants clipboard-read and clipboard-write, clicks "Copy invite link", then reads the clipboard to assert the exact URL was copied.

industries.problem: Join-call pages ask for camera and microphone access, and an unclickable browser prompt stalls tests unless permissions are granted up front.
Driver check-in pages depend on geolocation, so tests need preset coordinates and granted access to verify arrival detection without a real device.

cards.title: expect(locator).toBeVisible
cards.definition: Web-first assertion that retries until the element is visible or the timeout expires.
points: The assertion retries until it passes or the assertion timeout is reached.
Retrying assertions are async, so the docs require them to be awaited.
On timeout the error reports the last observed value, not just a failure.
useCases: Toast after save — a settings test clicks Save and awaits expect(toast).toBeVisible(), passing as soon as the notification mounts after the API call returns.
Modal after delete click — a test awaits expect(confirmDialog).toBeVisible() and reads the timeout error's last observed 'hidden' state when a dialog fails to open.

industries.problem: Transfer confirmation banners appear only after a slow backend call, and tests must prove the user actually sees the success message.
Cart drawers and out-of-stock notices render after async updates, so tests need to confirm the shopper can see them without fixed sleeps.

cards.title: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded
cards.definition: Scrolls to an element.
points: An element is scrolled into the viewport.
Actions scroll automatically, so this is for assertions and screenshots.
Virtualised lists may not render the element until it is scrolled.
useCases: Screenshot a footer legal notice — a test calls scrollIntoViewIfNeeded on the cookie and privacy links at the bottom of a long page so the full-page capture shows them in view.
Reveal a virtualised row before asserting — a table of 10,000 log entries only renders row 480 after scrolling, so the test scrolls its placeholder and then checks the row text.

industries.problem: Shipment tracking tables virtualise thousands of rows, so tests must scroll a row into view before it exists to assert its status.
Product pages place size guides and review sections far below the fold, and visual checks need them scrolled into view to be captured.

cards.title: getByLabel
cards.definition: Finds a form control by its associated label — the right way to reach inputs.
points: A form control is found through its associated label.
Going through the label is what proves the control is actually labelled.
An unlabelled input is invisible to this locator, which is the point.
useCases: Fill a login form by label — a test calls getByLabel('Password') to type into the credential field, which fails if the input has no associated label.
Reach a shipping address field — a checkout test uses getByLabel('Postal code') to enter a ZIP, so a label detached from its input breaks the test.

industries.problem: Checkout forms get redesigned often, and label-based lookup fails when a new input ships without a linked label.
Patient registration inputs must be labelled for screen readers, and getByLabel fails when a field has no accessible label.

cards.title: setInputFiles
cards.definition: Attaches files to a file input, including clearing it with an empty array.
points: Files are attached to a file input without a system dialog.
Bypassing the dialog is what makes uploads testable.
A custom uploader that hides the input needs the file chooser event.
useCases: Upload a profile avatar — a settings test passes a small PNG path to the file input and asserts the cropped preview thumbnail appears without opening the OS dialog.
Clear a chosen attachment — a support-ticket test attaches a PDF, then calls setInputFiles with an empty array and asserts the file name label disappears.

industries.problem: Claim forms require photo and PDF uploads, and tests must attach sample files directly to verify size and type validation messages.
New-hire portals use a drag-and-drop uploader with a hidden input, so tests need the file chooser event to submit ID documents.

cards.title: storageState
cards.definition: Saves and restores cookies and local storage, so tests start already signed in.
points: Cookies and origin storage are saved to a file and reused by later contexts.
`test.use({ storageState: { cookies: [], origins: [] } })` resets it for a signed-out test.
The official per-worker pattern keys the file by `test.info().parallelIndex`.
useCases: Share login across a worker — a fixture signs in once per parallelIndex, writes playwright/.auth/<index>.json, and reuses it so each parallel worker's account stays isolated.
Reuse a saved admin session — a setup project logs in as an admin once, saves cookies and localStorage to a file, and specs open the settings page already authenticated.

industries.problem: Hundreds of checkout and order-history tests would each repeat a slow login, so saved state lets them start signed in and run faster.
Workspace tests need a logged-in member with a token in localStorage, and restored storage avoids a sign-in on every board spec.

cards.title: Emulation
cards.definition: Device descriptors, locale, timezone, colour scheme, reduced motion and geolocation.
points: Viewport, device, locale, timezone and colour scheme are simulated.
Emulation is what tests responsive and localised behaviour.
It emulates the environment, not the device's real performance.
useCases: Dark mode and reduced motion — a test sets colorScheme to dark and reducedMotion to reduce, then asserts the dashboard theme applies and the slide-in animations are skipped.
Phone profile layout check — a test uses a device descriptor like iPhone 13 to confirm the checkout page stacks columns and shows touch-sized buttons at a narrow viewport.

industries.problem: Fare pages show dates, currency and local time per traveler, so emulated locales and timezones catch format bugs without real devices abroad.
Audits must confirm sites honor dark theme and reduced-motion preferences, which emulation toggles without changing any operating system setting.

cards.title: press
cards.definition: Sends a single key or chord, such as `Control+Enter`.
points: A single key or chord is sent to the focused element.
It is how Enter, Escape and shortcuts are exercised.
The element must be focused, which press does not do by itself.
useCases: Submit chat with Control+Enter — a support-widget test focuses the message textarea, types a reply, then presses Control+Enter to assert the message is sent and the box clears.
Dismiss modal with Escape — a test opens a settings dialog, presses Escape, and asserts the dialog closes and focus returns to the button that opened it.

industries.problem: Send and cancel shortcuts like Enter and Escape are core to chat, and only real key presses can confirm they trigger the right action.
Power users rely on keyboard chords to commit cells and navigate grids, so tests must send exact key combinations to the focused cell.

cards.title: chromium / firefox / webkit
cards.definition: The three bundled engines.
points: Three engines are bundled and driven through one API.
WebKit is the closest available proxy for Safari behaviour.
One API does not mean identical behaviour across the three.
useCases: Safari-only layout bug repro — a sticky checkout header overlaps the pay button in WebKit, so the test launches webkit alone to reproduce it before any fix.
Engine-specific date input check — a booking form's native date picker renders differently per engine, so assertions on its value format are verified in each of the three.

industries.problem: Many shoppers use Safari on iPhones and Macs, so WebKit runs catch checkout rendering bugs that Chromium-only testing misses.
Article pages with custom fonts, video embeds and CSS must look right in every engine, and the three engines expose engine-specific rendering differences.

cards.title: wait for network
cards.definition: Alias a route with cy.intercept() and wait for it with cy.wait('@alias') instead of sleeping for a guessed duration.
points: Set up the intercept and alias before visiting or performing the action that initiates the request, so the request cannot be missed.
Use cy.wait('@alias') to synchronize with completion of a matched request and its response.
The wait yields an object containing information about the matching request and response cycle, enabling targeted assertions.
useCases: Synchronize initial data loading — A page loads data after navigation.
Verify action-triggered requests — A click submits a form or triggers an API call.

industries.problem: Account balance tables fill from slow APIs, so waiting on the aliased request avoids asserting on stale or empty figures.
Appointment booking sends a POST, and waiting on it confirms the right patient and slot data were submitted before checking the UI.

cards.title: Debugging and retries
cards.definition: Cypress open mode combines a chronological Command Log, time-travel snapshots, and console details for diagnosing browser behavior.
points: Use the Command Log as the chronological index for commands and lifecycle hooks.
Select a command to correlate its subject, application state, and console output.
Hovering provides time-travel debugging without rerunning the test.
useCases: Separate flaky failures from deterministic failures — A test fails only intermittently in CI.
Time-travel through command states — A UI interaction produces an unexpected state.

industries.problem: Intermittent failures in transfer flows are hard to reproduce, so time-travel snapshots show the exact UI state at each step.
Appointment-booking tests break on dynamic forms, and console details reveal which element or value an assertion actually received.

source.label: Open mode in the Cypress app

cards.title: Screenshots and videos
cards.definition: Cypress can capture screenshots manually or automatically on test failure during `cypress run`.
points: Use `cy.screenshot()` when evidence is needed at a deliberate point in a test rather than only after failure.
Headless or CI runs provide automatic failure screenshots without adding screenshot commands to every test.
The screenshot output directory is configurable, with `cypress/screenshots` as the default.
useCases: Automatic failure evidence — A CI test fails and the team needs visual context without reproducing the failure locally.
Checkpoint screenshots — A test reaches a visually significant state such as a completed checkout or modal.

industries.problem: Intermittent checkout failures in CI are hard to diagnose, and a saved screenshot shows the exact error banner or missing payment field.
QA must show that consent screens and patient forms rendered correctly, so a screenshot at the final step gives reviewable evidence.

source.label: Capture screenshots and videos in Cypress

cards.title: Fixtures
cards.definition: Fixtures are reusable files containing static test data.
points: A fixture is a reusable, external data file that a test loads when needed.
Cypress uses cypress/fixtures by default, while fixturesFolder can point to a different location.
File extensions determine how supported fixture formats are parsed or encoded, including JSON, JavaScript, text, CSV, images, and ZIP files.
useCases: Deterministic network testing — Stub an API response with stable data so an end-to-end test does not depend on a live backend.
Shared test data — Reuse the same user, product, or configuration record across multiple tests without embedding it in each spec.

industries.problem: Patient portal tests need realistic lab-result payloads and sample documents without exposing real patient records.
Shipment tracking screens need fixed CSV manifests and tracking event data so route and status displays can be verified.

cards.title: cy.session
cards.definition: Cache and restore authenticated browser state so repeated tests can skip the login flow.
points: The command captures the browser's authentication state and restores it for later tests.
Setup runs for a new ID and runs again when the cached session is no longer valid.
Matching IDs let later tests avoid repeating the login setup.
useCases: Avoid repeated authentication — A suite repeatedly logs in through a form or API before each test.
Preserve the complete browser context — Authentication sets cookies or storage that must be available to each test.

industries.problem: Account dashboard specs need an MFA-protected login, and caching the session avoids repeating that slow flow in every test.
Multi-tenant admin consoles need tests as different roles, and cached sessions per role avoid logging in again for each spec.

cards.title: Request stubbing
cards.definition: Cypress request stubbing uses cy.intercept() to replace selected application HTTP responses with controlled bodies, statuses, headers, delays, or failures.
points: A stub can control the response body, status, headers, and delay.
Use cy.intercept() as the main command for matching and controlling application HTTP traffic.
A test may stub selected requests while allowing other matched traffic to reach the real server.
useCases: Simulate HTTP failures — Test application error handling without relying on a failing service.
Control response data — Make tests deterministic by replacing changing backend data with fixed fixtures or objects.

industries.problem: Transfer-failure and insufficient-funds screens can be tested by stubbing 4xx responses, with no real accounts touched.
Flight search UIs are checked against fixed fares and sold-out results that live airline APIs could not reproduce on demand.

cards.title: Component testing
cards.definition: Mount a component in Cypress's real browser, then interact with its rendered DOM and assert the visible result.
points: The component runs in a real browser rather than a simulated DOM, so rendering and browser behavior are exercised together.
The test runner displays the component while the test executes, making the rendered result directly observable.
Browser DevTools can help inspect the rendered component and troubleshoot both its implementation and the test.
useCases: Focused component behavior — Validate a component's user-facing behavior without starting the entire application.
Rendered interaction flows — Check that a click, input, or other browser action changes rendered UI state.

industries.problem: A product variant selector breaks only in real browsers, so mounting it alone catches size and color state bugs before checkout.
Shared buttons, modals and menus must behave the same across consuming apps, so each is tested in isolation in a real browser.

source.label: Get started with component testing | Cypress Documentation

cards.title: Fixtures and test data
cards.definition: Fixtures are checked-in static files that Cypress loads as controlled test data.
points: Fixtures establish a known input environment, helping repeated test runs produce comparable results.
Separate fixture files improve spec readability and let multiple tests reuse the same data.
Fixture files can use several formats, including JSON, JavaScript, HTML, text, CSV, images, and ZIP archives.
useCases: Stub network responses — A UI test needs predictable API data without contacting a live backend.
Reuse shared test data — Several specs use the same user, product, or API payload.

industries.problem: Checkout tests need the same cart, coupon and shipping-rate payloads each run, so price totals can be asserted without catalog changes breaking them.
Claim-intake forms need fixed policyholder records and sample attachments, so validation and upload flows can be tested without touching real customer data.

cards.title: Interacting with forms
cards.definition: Interact with a form by querying its controls, typing through them, asserting their values or outcomes, and submitting the form with `.submit()`.
points: Start submission from a DOM-query command, commonly `cy.get()`.
Assertions attached to the submission are retried and awaited by Cypress.
Target one form at a time; the submission command is not intended for multiple matched forms.
useCases: Form submission flow — Verify that a user can enter data and send a form.
Control-value validation — Confirm that text entered into a field is reflected in its value.

industries.problem: Multi-field quote forms break when validation rules change, so scripted entry and submit catches rejected input before release.
Public permit application forms must accept valid entries and show clear errors, which scripted submission checks on every build.

cards.title: Commands and chaining
cards.definition: Cypress commands are queued and chained through yielded subjects rather than executed immediately.
points: Calling a Cypress command queues it; execution happens after the test function has finished running.
Chaining lets Cypress coordinate command execution without requiring the test author to manage promises.
Queries inspect application state and provide subjects that later commands can use.
useCases: Reliable UI interaction — Locate an element, verify its state, then interact with it.
Inspection and assertions — Read application state and pass the yielded subject into assertions or later queries.

industries.problem: Shipment tracking tables re-render as statuses update, so chained queries re-find the row instead of holding a stale element.
Payroll forms show values only after earlier steps finish, and chaining keeps reads in order without hand-written promise code.

source.label: Table of Contents | Cypress API Documentation

cards.title: Network interception
cards.definition: Observe or stub requests with cy.intercept while keeping the tested contract visible.
points: cy.intercept observes or replaces a request while leaving the contract visible in the test.
Intercepting by route keeps the test readable when the call site moves.
An intercept registered after the request is made never matches it.
useCases: Watching a flow run and fail in a real browser — The time-travelling runner shows the application at each step, which turns a failed journey into an obvious cause.
Controlling what the backend returns — Stubbing requests makes error states, slow responses and empty results testable without a backend built to produce them.

industries.problem: Shipment tracking pages call a carrier route that moves between services, so intercepting by route keeps tests valid when the call site changes.
Search pages request fares from a pricing endpoint, and intercepting early shows the exact query sent before results render.

cards.title: Job outputs
cards.definition: Return named values from one GitHub Actions job so dependent jobs can consume them.
points: Job outputs provide a workflow-level way to transfer values between separate jobs.
Any downstream job that declares the producer as a dependency can consume its outputs.
Read a producer's values through the needs context in the dependent job.
useCases: Publish build metadata — A build job computes a version, digest, or artifact identifier that a later publishing job needs.
Gate a deployment — A validation job determines whether a deployment should proceed and exposes that decision to a dependent job.

industries.problem: A build job outputs the app version code so separate iOS and Android store-upload jobs tag releases identically.
A schema-detection job outputs which warehouse models changed so later jobs run migrations only for those models.

cards.title: Workflow files
cards.definition: A workflow is a versioned YAML file that defines when automation starts and what jobs and steps it performs.
points: Commit workflow definitions alongside source code so changes to automation are reviewable and versioned.
Use on to declare which repository activity starts the workflow.
A workflow must define at least one job, and each job is assigned execution to a runner.
useCases: Run tests when code is pushed or a pull request changes. — Continuous integration
Offer an operator-controlled workflow for tasks such as deployment. — Manual operations

industries.problem: Auditors need a reviewable history of who changed build and release automation, which committed workflow files provide through normal commits.
Dozens of microservice repos each need their own pipeline definition, so a workflow file in each repo lets teams change triggers independently.

cards.title: OIDC to cloud providers
cards.definition: GitHub Actions can use OIDC to obtain short-lived cloud access without storing long-lived credentials as GitHub secrets.
